status: Complete OpenITI Arabic witness; only selected paragraphs translated. Not a critically collated Arabic edition.

records.title: The transmitted sciences and the mixed character of jurisprudence
records.ar: ونقلي محض كالأحاديث والتفاسير، والخطب في أمثالها يسير؛ إذ يستوي في الاستقلال بها الصغير والكبير؛ لأن قوة الحفظ كافية في النقل وليس فيها مجال للعقل. وأشرف العلوم ما ازدوج فيه العقل والسمع واصطحب فيه الرأي والشرع، وعلم الفقه وأصوله من هذا القبيل فإنه يأخذ من صفو الشرع والعقل سواء السبيل، فلا هو تصرف بمحض العقول بحيث لا يتلقاه الشرع بالقبول ولا هو مبني على محض التقليد الذي لا يشهد له العقل بالتأييد والتسديد.
records.en: A second kind is purely transmitted, such as prophetic reports and Qurʾānic commentaries. The task involved in such disciplines is comparatively slight, since young and old can stand on equal footing in mastering them: strength of memory suffices for transmission, which, as such, affords no exercise to reason. The noblest sciences, however, are those in which intellect and transmitted authority are joined, and considered judgment accompanies revealed law. Jurisprudence and its principles belong to this class. They draw a straight course from the choicest elements of both revelation and reason. They are neither an exercise of unaided intellect which revelation cannot accept, nor a structure built upon mere imitation without the confirming and correcting witness of reason.
records.body: A new English translation of a consecutive Arabic paragraph from the identified OpenITI digital witness. Here al-ʿaql, al-samʿ, al-raʾy and al-sharʿ are four interrelated expressions and must not be flattened into a simple secular reason versus religious tradition opposition.

records.title: How al-Ghazālī situates his earlier writings
records.ar: ولأجل شرف علم الفقه وسببه وفر الله دواعي الخلق على طلبه وكان العلماء به أرفع العلماء مكانا وأجلهم شأنا وأكثرهم أتباعا وأعوانا؛ فتقاضاني في عنفوان شبابي اختصاص هذا العلم بفوائد الدين والدنيا وثواب الآخرة والأولى أن أصرف إليه من مهلة العمر صدرا وأن أخص به من متنفس الحياة قدرا، فصنفت كتبا كثيرة في فروع الفقه وأصوله، ثم أقبلت بعده على علم طريق الآخرة ومعرفة أسرار الدين الباطنة فصنفت فيه كتبا بسيطة ككتاب " إحياء علوم الدين " ووجيزة ككتاب جواهر القرآن ووسيطة ككتاب كيمياء السعادة.
records.en: Because of the excellence of jurisprudence and what gives it that excellence, God has made people eager to seek it; its scholars enjoy the highest rank and standing, and gather the greatest number of followers and supporters. In my early years, therefore, the distinctive benefits of this discipline for religion and worldly life, and the recompense of the next life and this, impelled me to devote the first portion of my allotted time to it and to reserve part of my remaining breath for its study. I composed many books on the detailed rulings of law and on its principles. Thereafter I turned to knowledge of the path to the afterlife and acquaintance with religion’s inward mysteries, and in that field composed extensive books, such as the Revival of the Religious Sciences, concise ones, such as The Jewels of the Qurʾān, and works of intermediate extent, such as The Alchemy of Happiness.

Hammad has not been systematically collated with this passage and any future critical text may require emendation. The three named works are securely identified by al-Ghazālī himself. Their being named here does not, by itself, establish a technical equivalence between their vocabulary and that of al-Mustaṣfā.

records.title: A deliberate middle course between earlier uṣūl works
records.ar: ثم ساقني قدر الله تعالى إلى معاودة التدريس والإفادة، فاقترح علي طائفة من محصلي علم الفقه تصنيفا في أصول الفقه أصرف العناية فيه إلى التلفيق بين الترتيب والتحقيق وإلى التوسط بين الإخلال والإملال على وجه يقع في الفهم دون كتاب " تهذيب الأصول " لميله إلى الاستقصاء والاستكثار، وفوق كتاب " المنخول " لميله إلى الإيجاز والاختصار، فأجبتهم إلى ذلك مستعينا بالله، وجمعت فيه بين الترتيب والتحقيق لفهم المعاني فلا مندوحة لأحدهما عن الثاني، فصنفته وأتيت فيه بترتيب لطيف عجيب يطلع الناظر في أول وهلة على جميع مقاصد هذا العلم ويفيده الاحتواء على جميع مسارح النظر فيه، فكل علم لا يستولي الطالب في ابتداء نظره على مجامعه ولا مبانيه فلا مطمع له في الظفر بأسراره ومباغيه؛ وقد سميته كتاب " المستصفى من علم الأصول والله تعالى هو المسئول لينعم بالتوفيق ويهدي إلى سواء الطريق وهو بإجابة السائلين حقيق.
records.en: God’s decree then brought me back to teaching and instruction. A group of advanced students of jurisprudence asked me to compose a treatise on legal theory in which I would unite systematic arrangement with rigorous examination, steering a middle course between a treatment too defective through omission and one too wearisome through excess. It was to be easier to grasp than The Refinement of Legal Principles, which inclines towards thoroughness and extensive treatment, but fuller than The Sifted Summary, which inclines towards brevity and condensation. I accepted their request with God’s assistance. I joined orderly arrangement to critical investigation, since the understanding of meanings cannot dispense with either. I therefore composed the work with an elegant and remarkable organization, so that at first sight the reader might grasp all the aims of the discipline and survey the entire field in which inquiry may proceed. Unless a student first gains command of a science’s principal divisions and foundations, there is no hope of reaching its deeper inquiries and ultimate goals. I have named it The Quintessence of the Science of Legal Principles [al-Mustaṣfā min ʿIlm al-Uṣūl]. It is God who is asked to grant success and guide us to the straight path; He is indeed the one who answers those who ask.

records.title: The opening: prolegomenon and four axes
records.ar: صدر الكتاب اعلم أن هذا العلم الملقب بأصول الفقه قد رتبناه وجمعناه في هذا الكتاب وبنيناه على مقدمة وأربعة أقطاب، المقدمة لها كالتوطئة والتمهيد، والأقطاب هي المشتملة على لباب المقصود. ولنذكر في صدر الكتاب معنى أصول الفقه وحده وحقيقته أولا، ثم مرتبته ونسبته إلى العلوم ثانيا، ثم كيفية انشعابه به إلى هذه المقدمة والأقطاب الأربعة ثالثا، ثم كيفية اندراج جميع أقسامه وتفاصيله تحت الأقطاب الأربعة رابعا، ثم وجه تعلقه بهذه المقدمة خامسا. بيان حد أصول الفقه
records.en: Opening of the book. Know that the discipline called the principles of jurisprudence has been ordered and collected in this book and built upon a preliminary introduction and four axes. The introduction serves as a preparation and preface, while the axes contain the substance of what is intended. At the outset we shall discuss, first, the meaning of uṣūl al-fiqh, its definition, and its reality; second, its standing and relation to the sciences; third, how it branches into this introduction and the four axes; fourth, how all its divisions and details fall under these four axes; and fifth, how it is related to the introduction. On defining the principles of jurisprudence.

The word quṭb here functions as the organizing axis or pivot of inquiry, not merely as a generic chapter or a metaphysical centre. The same classificatory structure is inherited and reworked in Ibn Rushd’s al-Ḍarūrī.

records.title: Technical fiqh versus ordinary understanding
records.ar: اعلم أنك لا تفهم معنى أصول الفقه ما لم تعرف أولا معنى الفقه، والفقه عبارة عن العلم والفهم في أصل الوضع، يقال فلان يفقه الخير والشر أي يعلمه ويفهمه، ولكن صار بعرف العلماء عبارة عن العلم بالأحكام الشرعية الثابتة لأفعال المكلفين خاصة، حتى لا يطلق بحكم العادة اسم الفقيه على متكلم وفلسفي ونحوي ومحدث ومفسر بل يختص بالعلماء بالأحكام الشرعية الثابتة للأفعال الإنسانية كالوجوب والحظر والإباحة والندب والكراهة وكون العقد صحيحا وفاسدا وباطلا وكون العبادة قضاء وأداء وأمثاله. ولا يخفى عليك أن للأفعال أحكاما عقلية أي مدركة بالعقل ككونها أعراضا وقائمة بالمحل ومخالفة للجوهر وكونها أكوانا حركة وسكونا وأمثالها، والعارف بذلك يسمى متكلما لا فقيها.
records.en: Understand that you cannot grasp the meaning of the principles of jurisprudence without first knowing what jurisprudence (fiqh) means. In its original linguistic sense, fiqh means knowledge and understanding: one says that a person understands good and evil, meaning that he knows and comprehends them. But in scholars’ established usage it has come to mean, specifically, knowledge of the revealed legal qualifications pertaining to the acts of those subject to the Law. Thus ordinary usage does not apply the name jurist (faqīh) to a theologian, philosopher, grammarian, scholar of transmitted reports, or exegete. It is reserved for those who know the legal qualifications of human acts—obligation, prohibition, permission, recommendation and reprehensibility; whether a contract is sound, defective, or void; whether an act of worship is performance within its time or discharge afterwards, and the like. You will also appreciate that acts have rationally ascertainable predicates, such as being accidents, inhering in a substrate, differing from substance, or constituting motion and rest. Someone who knows these is called a speculative theologian, not a jurist.

Translate aḥkām here as legal qualifications or legal rulings depending on grammatical context; do not take all these as properties inherent in the physical act. records.title: Uṣūl is about proof and indication at the general level
records.ar: وأما أحكامها من حيث إنها واجبة ومحظورة ومباحة ومكروهة ومندوب إليها فإنما يتولى الفقيه بيانها، فإذا فهمت هذا فافهم أن أصول الفقه عبارة عن أدلة هذه الأحكام وعن معرفة وجوه دلالتها على الأحكام من حيث الجملة لا من حيث التفصيل، فإن علم الخلاف من الفقه أيضا مشتمل على أدلة الأحكام ووجوه دلالتها ولكن من حيث التفصيل، كدلالة حديث خاص في مسألة النكاح بلا ولي على الخصوص ودلالة آية خاصة في مسألة متروك التسمية على الخصوص.
records.en: It is the jurist who explains the legal qualifications of acts as obligatory, forbidden, permitted, reprehensible, or recommended. Once you have understood that, understand also that uṣūl al-fiqh is concerned with the proofs of these rulings and with knowing the ways in which those proofs indicate the rulings—considered in general, not in the detailed treatment of particular cases. The discipline of juristic disagreement (ʿilm al-khilāf), which itself belongs to jurisprudence, likewise deals with the proofs of rulings and their modes of indication, but in relation to individual questions: for example, what a particular report indicates in the dispute over marriage without a guardian, or what a particular verse indicates for the case of slaughter without pronouncing God’s name.

This contrasts general modalities of legal evidence with evidential debate over particular rulings. It is not a contrast between theory that never uses concrete examples and practice that always does.

records.title: The three evidentiary foundations and methods of indication
records.ar: وأما الأصول فلا يتعرض فيها لإحدى المسائل ولا على طريق ضرب المثال، بل يتعرض فيها لأصل الكتاب والسنة والإجماع ولشرائط صحتها وثبوتها ثم لوجوه دلالتها الجملية إما من حيث صيغتها أو مفهوم لفظها أو مجرى لفظها أو معقول لفظها وهو القياس من غير أن يتعرض فيها لمسألة خاصة فبهذا تفارق أصول الفقه فروعه وقد عرفت من هذا أن أدلة الأحكام الكتاب والسنة والإجماع، فالعلم بطرق ثبوت هذه الأصول الثلاثة وشروط صحتها ووجوه دلالتها على الأحكام هو العلم الذي يعبر عنه بأصول الفقه
records.en: The principles, by contrast, do not take up an individual legal question as their subject, even in the manner of a worked example. Rather, their proper inquiry is into the foundation of the Book, the Sunna and consensus, the conditions of their authenticity and establishment, and then their general ways of indicating rulings: through linguistic form, through what the expression conveys by implication, through the course and requirements of the expression, or through the intelligible meaning discerned from it—that is, qiyās. They do not undertake the resolution of a particular legal question. This is what distinguishes the principles of jurisprudence from its branches. You can therefore see that the evidences of rulings are the Book, the Sunna and consensus; the discipline concerned with how these three foundations are established, with the conditions of their soundness, and with the ways in which they indicate rulings is what is meant by uṣūl al-fiqh.

Rather than impose “analogy” on every use of qiyās, translate it here according to its position among modes of textual indication. Opwis 2019, pp. 93–112, distinguishes inferential form from the epistemic standing of its premises.

records.title: The sciences and the discipline of inward purification
records.ar: اعلم أن العلوم تنقسم إلى عقلية كالطب والحساب والهندسة وليس ذلك من غرضنا. وإلى دينية كالكلام والفقه وأصوله وعلم الحديث وعلم التفسير وعلم الباطن، أعني علم القلب وتطهيره عن الأخلاق الذميمة وكل واحد من العقلية والدينية ينقسم إلى كلية وجزئية.
records.en: Understand that the sciences divide into rational disciplines, such as medicine, arithmetic and geometry—which are not our present concern—and religious disciplines, such as speculative theology (kalām), jurisprudence and its principles, the study of prophetic reports, Qurʾānic exegesis, and knowledge of the inward life: by the latter I mean knowledge of the heart and its purification from blameworthy character traits. Both the rational and the religious sciences can, in turn, be divided into comprehensive and particular disciplines.

The text expressly glosses “inward knowledge” as the science of the heart and its purification from blameworthy dispositions. Do not import a general esoteric doctrine merely from the expression.

records.title: Why kalām is classed as comprehensive
records.ar: فالعلم الكلي من العلوم الدينية هو الكلام وسائر العلوم من الفقه وأصوله والحديث والتفسير علوم جزئية، لأن المفسر لا ينظر إلا في معنى الكتاب خاصة والمحدث لا ينظر إلا في طريق ثبوت الحديث خاصة، والفقيه لا ينظر إلا في أحكام أفعال المكلفين خاصة، والأصولي لا ينظر إلا في أدلة الأحكام الشرعية خاصة والمتكلم هو الذي ينظر في أعم الأشياء وهو الموجود، فيقسم الموجود أولا إلى قديم حادث، ثم يقسم المحدث إلى جوهر وعرض، ثم يقسم العرض إلى ما تشترط فيه الحياة من العلم والإرادة والقدرة والكلام والسمع والبصر وإلى ما يستغني عنها كاللون والريح والطعم، ويقسم الجوهر إلى الحيوان والنبات والجماد ويبين أن اختلافها بالأنواع أو بالأعراض.
records.en: Within the religious sciences, kalām is the comprehensive discipline; the others—jurisprudence, its principles, the science of reports and exegesis—are particular sciences. For the exegete considers specifically the meaning of the Book; the traditionist the way in which a report is established; the jurist the legal qualifications of the acts of those subject to the Law; and the uṣūlī the proofs of revealed rulings. The speculative theologian, by contrast, considers what is most universal: being (al-mawjūd). He first divides what exists into eternal and originated; then originated being into substance and accident; then accidents into those requiring life—such as knowledge, will, power, speech, hearing and sight—and those not requiring it, such as colour, smell and taste. He divides substances into animals, plants and inanimate bodies, and examines whether their distinctions are differences of species or of accidents.

Al-mawjūd, jawhar and ʿaraḍ are technical terms in Ashʿarī kalām, not direct equivalents of Heideggerian Being or the Aristotelian substance-accident contrast without historical qualification.

records.title: The relative autonomy of legal theory
records.ar: فإذا الكلام هو المتكفل بإثبات مبادئ العلوم الدينية كلها، فهي جزئية بالإضافة إلى الكلام، فالكلام هو العلم الأعلى في الرتبة إذ منه النزول إلى هذه الجزئيات فإن قيل: فليكن من شرط الأصولي والفقيه والمفسر والمحدث أن يكون قد حصل علم الكلام لأنه قبل الفراغ من الكلي الأعلى كيف يمكنه النزول إلى الجزئي الأسفل؟ قلنا: ليس ذلك شرطا في كونه أصوليا وفقيها ومفسرا ومحدثا وإن كان ذلك شرطا في كونه عالما مطلقا مليئا بالعلوم الدينية، وذلك أنه ما من علم من العلوم الجزئية إلا وله مباد تؤخذ مسلمة بالتقليد في ذلك العلم ويطلب برهان ثبوتها في علم آخر.
records.en: Kalām, then, undertakes to establish the first principles of all the religious sciences, which are particular in relation to it. In this respect kalām ranks as the highest of the sciences, since one descends from it to these particular disciplines. An objection may be raised: Should it not then be a condition of being an uṣūlī, jurist, exegete or traditionist that one have mastered kalām? How could someone descend to a lower, particular science without first completing the higher, comprehensive one? We reply: this is not a condition for being an uṣūlī, jurist, exegete or traditionist, though it is a condition for being a scholar in the unrestricted sense, fully equipped with the religious sciences. Every particular science has first principles accepted as given within it, whose demonstration is sought in some other science.

The acceptance of a premise inside one science does not establish that it cannot be demonstratively justified elsewhere.

records.title: The jurist’s and uṣūlī’s borrowed premises
records.ar: فالفقيه ينظر في نسبة فعل المكلف إلى خطاب الشرع في أمره ونهيه وليس عليه إقامة البرهان على إثبات الأفعال الاختياريات للمكلفين فقد أنكرت الجبرية فعل الإنسان وأنكرت طائفة وجود الأعراض والفعل عرض. ولا على الفقيه إقامة البرهان على ثبوت خطاب الشرع وأن لله تعالى كلاما قائما بنفسه هو أمر ونهي، ولكن يأخذ ثبوت الخطاب من الله تعالى وثبوت الفعل من المكلف على سبيل التقليد وينظر في نسبة الفعل إلى الخطاب فيكون قد قام بمنتهى علمه. وكذلك الأصولي يأخذ بالتقليد من المتكلم أن قول الرسول حجة ودليل واجب الصدق، ثم ينظر في وجوه دلالته وشروط صحته.
records.en: The jurist investigates the relation of a legally accountable person’s act to the Law’s address, commanding or forbidding it. He is not required to demonstrate that human beings perform voluntary acts—although the determinists have denied human agency, while another group has denied accidents, and an act is an accident. Nor is the jurist obliged to prove the existence of a revealed legal address or the doctrine that God possesses speech subsisting in Him which commands and forbids. Instead, he takes as granted the existence of God’s address and the act of the accountable person, and studies the relation between them. In doing so he has reached the proper terminus of his discipline. Likewise, the uṣūlī accepts from the theologian, without himself demonstrating it there, that the Messenger’s utterance is authoritative proof whose truth must be acknowledged; he then investigates its modes of indication and the conditions of its authenticity.

Taqlīd here means taking a science’s borrowed foundations as granted for the purposes of its specific inquiry, not a blanket rejection of reason. The paragraph’s theological doctrines are al-Ghazālī’s claims, not editorial endorsements.

records.title: The four parts follow from derivation itself
records.ar: بيان كيفية دورانه على الأقطاب الأربعة اعلم أنك إذا فهمت أن نظر الأصولي في وجوه دلالة الأدلة السمعية على الأحكام الشرعية لم يخف عليك أن المقصود معرفة كيفية اقتباس الأحكام من الأدلة، فوجب النظر في الأحكام، ثم في الأدلة وأقسامها، ثم في كيفية اقتباس الأحكام من الأدلة، ثم في صفات المقتبس الذي له أن يقتبس الأحكام، فإن الأحكام ثمرات وكل ثمرة فلها صفة وحقيقة في نفسها ولها مثمر ومستثمر وطريق في الاستثمار.
records.en: On how the science turns upon its four axes. Once you understand that the uṣūlī investigates how transmitted proofs indicate legal rulings, you will see that the object is to know how to draw rulings from their proofs. We must therefore consider, first, the rulings themselves; second, the proofs and their classes; third, how rulings are drawn from proofs; and fourth, the qualities of the one entitled to draw them. For rulings are fruits, and every fruit has a character and nature of its own, a source that produces it, someone who harvests it, and a manner of harvesting.

The image distinguishes object, authoritative evidence, inferential technique, and qualified knower; it does not mean that there are four coequal original sources of law.

records.title: The fruits, the productive proofs, and the modes of drawing them
records.ar: والثمرة هي الأحكام، أعني الوجوب والحظر والندب والكراهة والإباحة والحسن والقبح والقضاء والأداء والصحة والفساد وغيرها والمثمر هي الأدلة، وهي ثلاثة الكتاب والسنة والإجماع فقط. وطرق الاستثمار هي وجوه دلالة الأدلة وهي أربعة، إذ الأقوال إما أن تدل على الشيء بصيغتها ومنظومها، أو بفحواها ومفهومها وباقتضائها وضرورتها أو بمعقولها ومعناها المستنبط منها.
records.en: The fruits are the rulings: obligation, prohibition, recommendation, reprehensibility, permission, the good and the bad, compensatory performance and timely performance, legal soundness and defectiveness, and other such qualifications. The productive sources are the proofs, and these are three only: the Book, the Sunna and consensus. The ways of harvesting are the modes by which proofs indicate their conclusions, and these are four: utterances indicate something either through their linguistic form and expressed wording; through what their sense and implication convey; through what they necessarily require or presuppose; or through the intelligible meaning inferred from them.
records.body: A new English translation of a consecutive Arabic paragraph from the identified OpenITI digital witness. Hammad has not been systematically collated with this passage and any future critical text may require emendation. The source organizes four modes of signification. Do not assimilate these without qualification to a single modern linguistic taxonomy or to a claim that every example yields deductive certainty.

records.title: The jurist as harvester and the four axes
records.ar: والمستثمر هو المجتهد، ولا بد من معرفة صفاته وشروطه وأحكامه. فإذا جملة الأصول تدور على أربعة أقطاب: القطب الأول: في الأحكام، والبداءة بها أولى لأنها الثمرة المطلوبة. القطب الثاني: في الأدلة، وهي الكتاب والسنة والإجماع وبها التثنية إذ بعد الفراغ من معرفة الثمرة لا أهم من معرفة المثمر. القطب الثالث: في طريق الاستثمار، وهو وجوه دلالة الأدلة، وهي أربعة: دلالة بالمنظوم، ودلالة بالمفهوم، ودلالة بالضرورة والاقتضاء، ودلالة بالمعنى المعقول. القطب الرابع: في المستثمر وهو المجتهد الذي يحكم بظنه، ويقابله المقلد الذي يلزمه اتباعه، فيجب ذكر شروط المقلد والمجتهد وصفاتهما.
records.en: The harvester is the independent jurist (mujtahid), whose qualities, conditions and legal position must be known. Accordingly, the entire discipline of legal theory turns upon four axes. The first concerns rulings; we begin with them because they are the fruit sought. The second concerns the proofs—the Book, the Sunna and consensus. They come second because, once the fruit is known, nothing is more important than knowing the source that produces it. The third concerns the manner of harvesting, that is, the modes of indication of proofs: indication through explicit wording, through implication, through necessary presupposition and entailment, and through an intelligible inferred meaning. The fourth concerns the harvester, the mujtahid, who renders judgment according to his preponderant estimation (ẓann). Opposite him stands the follower (muqallid), who is bound to follow the jurist. We must therefore discuss the conditions and qualifications of both.
records.body: A new English translation of a consecutive Arabic paragraph from the identified OpenITI digital witness. Hammad has not been systematically collated with this passage and any future critical text may require emendation. The expression yaḥkumu bi-ẓannihi should be rendered as a ruling reached on the basis of predominant yet fallible judgment, not as an arbitrary guess. Compare Opwis (2019), 103–108, and Hallaq’s discussion of legal epistemology.

records.title: The four axes comprehend the scattered chapters of uṣūl
records.ar: لعلك تقول أصول الفقه تشتمل على أبواب كثيرة وفصول منتشرة فكيف يندرج جملتها تحت هذه الأقطاب الأربعة؟ فنقول: القطب الأول: هو الحكم.
records.en: You might ask: “The principles of jurisprudence contain many chapters and dispersed subdivisions. How can all of them fall under these four axes?” We reply: the first axis concerns the legal ruling (al-ḥukm).
records.body: Al-Ghazālī is offering a disciplinary architecture, not presenting four independent material sources of the law.

records.title: Ruler, addressee, subject act, and manifestation of the ruling
records.ar: وللحكم حقيقة في نفسه وانقسام، وله تعلق بالحاكم وهو الشارع والمحكوم عليه وهو المكلف وبالمحكوم فيه وهو فعل المكلف وبالمظهر له وهو السبب والعلة
records.en: A ruling has a determinate nature and divisions of its own. It is related to the one who lays it down—the Lawgiver (al-shāriʿ); the one upon whom it bears—the legally accountable person (al-mukallaf); that with which it is concerned—the accountable person’s act; and that by which it is made manifest—the occasioning condition (sabab) and the operative ground (ʿilla).
records.body: The sequence is an analytic ordering of the ruling’s relations. Here sabab and ʿilla are connected with the manifestation of a rule; translating both as physical “cause” would mislead. This is an excerpt from a longer sentence; the remaining subdivisions are not silently paraphrased as though translated here.

records.title: The ruling is an address of revelation, not an attribute of the act
records.ar: ففي البحث عن حقيقة الحكم في نفسه يتبين أنه عبارة عن خطاب الشرع وليس وصفا للفعل ولا حسن ولا قبح ولا مدخل للعقل فيه ولا حكم قبل ورود الشرع
records.en: Investigation of the ruling’s nature shows that it consists in the address of revealed law (khiṭāb al-sharʿ), not in a quality belonging to the act itself—neither its goodness nor its badness. Reason does not constitute this ruling, and no such revealed-law ruling obtains before revelation has come.
records.body: The denial concerns constituting a binding revealed-law classification; it should not be generalized into a denial that reason recognizes truths or consequences of actions. Compare the chapter on ḥusn and qubḥ before revelation.

records.title: Required implication: what an utterance must presuppose
records.ar: وأما الدلالة من حيث ضرورة اللفظ واقتضاؤه فيتضمن جملة من إشارات الألفاظ كقول القائل: أعتق عبدك عني، فتقول: أعتقت، فإنه يتضمن حصول الملك للملتمس ولم يتلفظا به لكنه من ضرورة ملفوظهما ومقتضاه.
records.en: Indication through what an utterance necessarily presupposes and requires includes certain implications of what has been said. Suppose someone says: “Emancipate your slave on my behalf,” and you reply: “I have emancipated him.” These words entail the requester’s acquiring ownership, although neither speaker expressly mentioned it; that transfer is demanded by what they have uttered.
records.body: The inferred transaction is required for the utterance to be legally intelligible, rather than expressly stated in its words. “Implied meaning” without this necessity would be too broad.

records.title: Intelligible meaning and extension beyond the stated case
records.ar: وأما الدلالة من حيث معقول اللفظ فهو كقوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: «لا يقضي القاضي وهو غضبان» فإنه يدل على الجائع والمريض والحاقن بمعقول معناه، ومنه ينشأ القياس وينجر إلى بيان جميع أحكام القياس وأقسامه.
records.en: Indication through the intelligible import of an utterance is exemplified by the Prophet’s saying: “A judge must not adjudicate while angry.” Through its intelligible ground, the instruction extends also to someone distracted by hunger, illness, or an urgent need to relieve himself. From this sort of indication arises juridical qiyās, and from it follows the examination of the rulings and kinds of qiyās.
records.body: The extension is not a literal occurrence of the words “hunger” or “illness.” It rests on discerning the relevant ground and transferring the ruling. Compare the discussion of legal analogy and syllogistic form in Felicitas Opwis, “Syllogistic Logic in Islamic Legal Theory.”

records.title: The triad of knowledge, proof, and ruling
records.ar: اعلم أنه لما رجع حد أصول الفقه إلى معرفة أدلة الأحكام اشتمل الحد على ثلاثة ألفاظ: المعرفة والدليل والحكم فقالوا: إذا لم يكن بد من معرفة الحكم حتى كان معرفته أحد الأقطاب الأربعة فلا بد أيضا من معرفة الدليل ومعرفة المعرفة، أعني العلم. ثم العلم المطلوب لا وصول إليه إلا بالنظر، فلا بد من معرفة النظر
records.en: Understand that, once the definition of uṣūl al-fiqh had been reduced to knowing the proofs of legal rulings, it contained three terms: knowledge, proof, and ruling. It was therefore argued that, just as a ruling must be understood—indeed, knowledge of rulings is one of the four axes—one must also understand proof and what it is to know, namely, knowledge (ʿilm). The knowledge sought here, moreover, is reached only by disciplined inquiry (naẓar), so inquiry too must be understood.
records.body: Naẓar is disciplined intellectual investigation; rendering it simply as “vision” or as an unqualified “rationalism” would suppress its methodological sense.

records.title: Which questions properly belong to uṣūl?
records.ar: وأما معرفة حجية الإجماع وحجية القياس فذلك من خاصية أصول الفقه
records.en: Establishing the probative authority (ḥujjiyya) of consensus (ijmāʿ) and of qiyās, by contrast, belongs specifically to the discipline of uṣūl al-fiqh.
records.body: A proof’s status as authoritative is a distinct question from the formal validity of an argument or the certainty of a premise.

records.title: Why a logical introduction is nevertheless retained
records.ar: لكنا نقتصر من ذلك على ما تظهر فائدته على العموم في جملة العلوم من تعريف مدارك العقول وكيفية تدرجها من الضروريات إلى النظريات على وجه يتبين فيه حقيقة العلم والنظر والدليل وأقسامها وحججها تبيينا بليغا تخلو عنه مصنفات الكلام.
records.en: We shall, however, confine ourselves to what has evident general benefit across the sciences: setting out the intellect’s modes of apprehension and the manner in which it advances from immediate or necessary cognitions (ḍarūriyyāt) to matters established through investigation (naẓariyyāt). This will clarify the nature of knowledge, inquiry, and proof, together with their divisions and warrants, more fully than is ordinarily found in works of kalām.
records.body: This passage explains why the logical introduction is useful generally. It is not a claim that all the material in that introduction belongs intrinsically to legal theory.

records.title: Three kinds of knowledge
records.ar: ثم العلوم ثلاثة: عقلي محض لا يحث الشرع عليه ولا يندب إليه كالحساب والهندسة والنجوم وأمثاله من العلوم
records.en: There are, then, three kinds of sciences. One is purely rational, and is not, as such, urged or recommended by the revealed Law—for example, arithmetic, geometry, and astronomy.
records.body: Read the surrounding passage: he distinguishes uncertain speculation from true knowledge lacking the benefit relevant to his argument; this is not an assessment of every mathematical practice.

records.title: Knowledge transmitted without inference
records.ar: ونقلي محض كالأحاديث والتفاسير، والخطب في أمثالها يسير؛ إذ يستوي في الاستقلال بها الصغير والكبير؛ لأن قوة الحفظ كافية في النقل
records.en: Another kind is purely transmitted, such as reports and commentarial traditions. Its acquisition, considered solely as transmission, demands little by way of argument: young and old alike can master it, since retention suffices for conveying it.
records.body: The claim concerns mere transmission, not every interpretative discipline of hadith or tafsīr.

records.title: The value of legal theory as a mixed science
records.ar: وأشرف العلوم ما ازدوج فيه العقل والسمع واصطحب فيه الرأي والشرع
records.en: The noblest sciences are those in which reason and transmitted revelation are joined, and considered judgment accompanies the revealed Law.
records.body: Compare his explicit acknowledgement of the inward sciences later in the preface rather than artificially opposing law to ethical or spiritual knowledge.

records.title: The meeting of reason and revelation
records.ar: وأشرف العلوم ما ازدوج فيه العقل والسمع واصطحب فيه الرأي والشرع، وعلم الفقه وأصوله من هذا القبيل فإنه يأخذ من صفو الشرع والعقل سواء السبيل، فلا هو تصرف بمحض العقول بحيث لا يتلقاه الشرع بالقبول ولا هو مبني على محض التقليد الذي لا يشهد له العقل بالتأييد والتسديد.
records.en: The noblest sciences are those in which reason and received revelation are joined, and reflective judgment accompanies the revealed Law. Jurisprudence and its principles belong to this kind: drawing from the clearest part of both revelation and reason, they follow an even course. They are neither an operation of unaided intellect that revelation would refuse to recognize, nor something resting on mere imitation without the confirmation and guidance of reason.
records.body: Al-Ghazālī juxtaposes four distinct terms. “Received revelation” renders samʿ here, in contrast with rational inquiry; it must not be silently reduced to isolated textual citations. The juxtaposition is authored in the preface and bears directly on comparisons with the logical and ethical works. Hammad renders samʿ as “Tradition” and raʾy as rational opinion. This new rendering uses “received revelation” for samʿ and “reflective judgment” for raʾy to preserve both contrasts with ʿaql and sharʿ. The proposal is open to revision when the Arabic edition is fixed; it is not a correction of Hammad’s interpretation by fiat.

records.title: Earlier theological, juristic, and spiritual writing
records.ar: فصنفت كتبا كثيرة في فروع الفقه وأصوله، ثم أقبلت بعده على علم طريق الآخرة ومعرفة أسرار الدين الباطنة فصنفت فيه كتبا بسيطة ككتاب إحياء علوم الدين ووجيزة ككتاب جواهر القرآن ووسيطة ككتاب كيمياء السعادة.
records.en: I composed numerous books on the branches of jurisprudence and on its principles. I then turned to knowledge of the path to the Hereafter and the inward secrets of religion, producing expansive books in that field, such as the Revival of the Religious Sciences; concise books, such as The Jewels of the Qurʾān; and intermediate works, such as The Alchemy of Happiness.
records.body: The Iḥyāʾ, Jawāhir al-Qurʾān, and Kīmiyā-yi Saʿādat are named by al-Ghazālī in his own preface; these links are direct bibliographic evidence, not terminology-equivalence claims.

records.title: Between excessive length and excessive brevity
records.ar: فاقترح علي طائفة من محصلي علم الفقه تصنيفا في أصول الفقه أصرف العناية فيه إلى التلفيق بين الترتيب والتحقيق وإلى التوسط بين الإخلال والإملال على وجه يقع في الفهم دون كتاب تهذيب الأصول لميله إلى الاستقصاء والاستكثار، وفوق كتاب المنخول لميله إلى الإيجاز والاختصار.
records.en: A group of students accomplished in jurisprudence asked me for a work on legal principles that would unite careful arrangement with rigorous examination, and hold a middle course between harmful omission and wearisome elaboration. They wanted something accessible to understanding: less expansive than the Refinement of the Principles, which inclines to exhaustive treatment, but fuller than the Sifted Work, which inclines toward compression and brevity.
records.body: Al-Ghazālī explicitly compares the scope of al-Mustaṣfā with his Tahdhīb al-Uṣūl and al-Mankhūl, inviting diachronic collation of terminology and method.

records.title: The design of the book
records.ar: اعلم أن هذا العلم الملقب بأصول الفقه قد رتبناه وجمعناه في هذا الكتاب وبنيناه على مقدمة وأربعة أقطاب، المقدمة لها كالتوطئة والتمهيد، والأقطاب هي المشتملة على لباب المقصود.
records.en: Know that we have organized and assembled in this book the discipline called the principles of jurisprudence. We have built it upon an introduction and four principal axes. The introduction serves as preparation and groundwork, while the axes contain the substance of what we seek to establish.
records.body: The axes (aqṭāb) organize relations among rule, evidence, inference, and the jurist, rather than simply listing types of evidence. Compare Hammad’s rendering “four Qutbs [poles]”. The present edition translates the term as “principal axes” while retaining quṭb in the glossary. This is an editorial choice, not a textual variant.

records.title: The five introductory questions
records.ar: ولنذكر في صدر الكتاب معنى أصول الفقه وحده وحقيقته أولا، ثم مرتبته ونسبته إلى العلوم ثانيا، ثم كيفية انشعابه إلى هذه المقدمة والأقطاب الأربعة ثالثا، ثم كيفية اندراج جميع أقسامه وتفاصيله تحت الأقطاب الأربعة رابعا، ثم وجه تعلقه بهذه المقدمة خامسا.
records.en: At the outset, then, we shall first set out the meaning, definition, and reality of the principles of jurisprudence; second, their rank and relation to the other sciences; third, how this science branches into the introduction and the four axes; fourth, how all its parts and details fall under those axes; and fifth, how the introduction relates to the discipline itself.

records.title: From fiqh as understanding to fiqh as jurisprudence
records.ar: اعلم أنك لا تفهم معنى أصول الفقه ما لم تعرف أولا معنى الفقه، والفقه عبارة عن العلم والفهم في أصل الوضع، يقال فلان يفقه الخير والشر أي يعلمه ويفهمه، ولكن صار بعرف العلماء عبارة عن العلم بالأحكام الشرعية الثابتة لأفعال المكلفين خاصة.
records.en: Understand that you cannot grasp the meaning of the principles of jurisprudence without first knowing what jurisprudence itself means. In its original linguistic use, fiqh signifies knowledge and understanding: to say that someone understands good and evil is to say that he knows and comprehends them. In scholars’ established usage, however, fiqh has come to mean specifically knowledge of the rulings of the revealed Law attaching to the acts of those subject to obligation.
records.body: The movement from lexical “understanding” to the technical discipline is part of the argument; the two senses must not be collapsed.

records.title: The distinct object of jurisprudence
records.ar: حتى لا يطلق بحكم العادة اسم الفقيه على متكلم وفلسفي ونحوي ومحدث ومفسر بل يختص بالعلماء بالأحكام الشرعية الثابتة للأفعال الإنسانية كالوجوب والحظر والإباحة والندب والكراهة وكون العقد صحيحا وفاسدا وباطلا وكون العبادة قضاء وأداء وأمثاله.
records.en: Custom therefore does not call a theologian, philosopher, grammarian, hadith specialist, or exegete a jurist simply on account of that expertise. The term is reserved for those who know the legal rulings that attach to human actions: obligation, prohibition, permission, recommendation, and reprehensibility; whether a contract is sound, defective, or void; and whether an act of worship is performed at its prescribed time or made up afterward, and other such questions.
records.body: “Sound,” “defective,” and “void” are preserved as distinct terms. Their doctrinal relation cannot be assumed to be identical across the Shāfiʿī and Ḥanafī schools.

records.title: Rational predicates versus legal qualifications
records.ar: ولا يخفى عليك أن للأفعال أحكاما عقلية أي مدركة بالعقل ككونها أعراضا وقائمة بالمحل ومخالفة للجوهر وكونها أكوانا حركة وسكونا وأمثالها، والعارف بذلك يسمى متكلما لا فقيها.
records.en: It will not escape you that actions also have predicates knowable by reason: that they are accidents, subsist in a subject, differ from substance, or belong to the kinds of occurrence called motion and rest. Someone versed in these matters is called a theologian, not a jurist.
records.body: In this sentence aḥkām can mean intelligible predicates or determinations. In the immediately following passage it means normative legal qualifications. A uniform English “rules” would obscure al-Ghazālī’s contrast.

records.title: What uṣūl actually investigates
records.ar: وأما أحكامها من حيث إنها واجبة ومحظورة ومباحة ومكروهة ومندوب إليها فإنما يتولى الفقيه بيانها، فإذا فهمت هذا فافهم أن أصول الفقه عبارة عن أدلة هذه الأحكام وعن معرفة وجوه دلالتها على الأحكام من حيث الجملة لا من حيث التفصيل.
records.en: The jurist, by contrast, explains the qualifications of acts insofar as they are obligatory, forbidden, permitted, disapproved, or recommended. Once you grasp this, understand that uṣūl al-fiqh concerns the proofs for such rulings, together with knowledge of the ways in which those proofs indicate rulings considered generally, not in the particular detail of each disputed case.
records.body: “Indication” is deliberate: a source’s evidentiary force is not equivalent to its merely containing an English statement of the ruling.

records.title: General principles and particular cases
records.ar: وأما الأصول فلا يتعرض فيها لإحدى المسائل ولا على طريق ضرب المثال، بل يتعرض فيها لأصل الكتاب والسنة والإجماع ولشرائط صحتها وثبوتها ثم لوجوه دلالتها الجملية إما من حيث صيغتها أو مفهوم لفظها أو مجرى لفظها أو معقول لفظها وهو القياس من غير أن يتعرض فيها لمسألة خاصة.
records.en: As for the principles, they do not treat a specific legal problem as their subject, even for the sake of expounding its details. Rather, they investigate the Qurʾān, the Sunna, and consensus as foundational proofs, the conditions under which each is established and sound, and the general modes of their indication: by the form of an expression, by what is understood from its wording, by the course of its wording, or by its intelligible sense—the last being analogy—without examining any particular disputed issue.
records.body: This passage distinguishes subject matter and method. Al-Ghazālī uses examples throughout the book but refuses to make a particular fiqh ruling the object of uṣūl.

records.title: What counts as uṣūl
records.ar: فأصول الفقه عبارة عن أدلة هذه الأحكام وعن معرفة وجوه دلالتها على الأحكام من حيث الجملة لا من حيث التفصيل
records.en: Uṣūl al-fiqh consists of the proofs of these rulings, together with knowledge of the general ways in which those proofs indicate rulings—not the examination of every detailed case.
records.body: Min ḥayth al-jumla is a methodological restriction on the discipline, not a claim that detailed rulings are irrelevant to its application.

records.title: The three established textual sources
records.ar: وقد عرفت من هذا أن أدلة الأحكام الكتاب والسنة والإجماع
records.en: You can now see that the proofs of rulings are the Book, the Sunna, and consensus.
records.body: The fourth discussion, inference from these proofs, is developed as a method of deriving conclusions, not necessarily as a coequal new revelatory source.

records.title: Religious sciences include an inward science
records.ar: وإلى دينية كالكلام والفقه وأصوله وعلم الحديث وعلم التفسير وعلم الباطن، أعني علم القلب وتطهيره عن الأخلاق الذميمة، وكل واحد من العقلية والدينية ينقسم إلى كلية وجزئية.
records.en: Other sciences are religious: theology, jurisprudence and its principles, the science of prophetic reports, Qurʾānic interpretation, and the inward science—by which I mean knowledge of the heart and its purification from blameworthy dispositions. Both the rational and the religious sciences divide into universal and particular disciplines.
records.body: The inward discipline is expressly included in this taxonomy. The hierarchy developed in the next paragraph concerns the generality of the subject investigated, not the worth of a life devoted to the science.

records.title: The disciplinary domain of theology and law
records.ar: فالعلم الكلي من العلوم الدينية هو الكلام وسائر العلوم من الفقه وأصوله والحديث والتفسير علوم جزئية، لأن المفسر لا ينظر إلا في معنى الكتاب خاصة، والمحدث لا ينظر إلا في طريق ثبوت الحديث خاصة، والفقيه لا ينظر إلا في أحكام أفعال المكلفين خاصة، والأصولي لا ينظر إلا في أدلة الأحكام الشرعية خاصة، والمتكلم هو الذي ينظر في أعم الأشياء وهو الموجود.
records.en: Among the religious sciences, theology is the universal discipline, while jurisprudence, its principles, reports, and exegesis are particular disciplines. The exegete investigates the meaning of the Book as such; the traditionist examines the means by which a report is established; the jurist examines rulings governing the acts of those under legal obligation; the uṣūlī examines the evidence for legal rulings; and the theologian investigates the most general object of all, namely what exists.
records.body: Do not translate kullī as if Ghazālī were calling kalām universally true and fiqh merely local. His criterion here is extension of the field of inquiry.

records.title: Rational and religious sciences
records.ar: اعلم أن العلوم تنقسم إلى عقلية كالطب والحساب والهندسة وليس ذلك من غرضنا، وإلى دينية كالكلام والفقه وأصوله وعلم الحديث وعلم التفسير وعلم الباطن أعني علم القلب وتطهيره عن الأخلاق الذميمة وكل واحد من العقلية والدينية ينقسم إلى كلية وجزئية.
records.en: Know that the sciences divide into rational disciplines, such as medicine, arithmetic, and geometry—which do not concern us here—and religious disciplines, such as theology, jurisprudence and its principles, the science of hadith, Qurʾānic exegesis, and the inward science, by which I mean the science of the heart and its purification from blameworthy dispositions. Both rational and religious sciences may be divided into universal and particular.
records.body: The science of the heart is explicitly included in this classification. Comparison with the Iḥyāʾ on knowledge and cultivation is warranted, but no terminological identity has been presumed.

records.title: Why kalām is universal here
records.ar: فالعلم الكلي من العلوم الدينية هو الكلام وسائر العلوم من الفقه وأصوله والحديث والتفسير علوم جزئية، لأن المفسر لا ينظر إلا في معنى الكتاب خاصة والمحدث لا ينظر إلا في طريق ثبوت الحديث خاصة والفقيه لا ينظر إلا في أحكام أفعال المكلفين خاصة والأصولي لا ينظر إلا في أدلة الأحكام الشرعية خاصة.
records.en: Among the religious sciences it is kalām that is universal. The others—jurisprudence and its principles, hadith, and exegesis—are particular: the exegete investigates the meaning of the Book; the hadith scholar, the means by which a report is established; the jurist, the rulings concerning the acts of accountable persons; and the uṣūl specialist, the evidence for those legal rulings.
records.body: His claim concerns the level of generality of kalām’s object, not that every jurist is personally required to prove every theological premise.

records.title: From evidence to derivation
records.ar: اعلم أنك إذا فهمت أن نظر الأصولي في وجوه دلالة الأدلة السمعية على الأحكام الشرعية لم يخف عليك أن المقصود معرفة كيفية اقتباس الأحكام من الأدلة، فوجب النظر في الأحكام ثم في الأدلة وأقسامها ثم في كيفية اقتباس الأحكام من الأدلة ثم في صفات المقتبس الذي له أن يقتبس الأحكام.
records.en: Once you understand that the theorist of uṣūl investigates how transmitted proofs indicate legal rulings, you will see that the aim is to know how rulings are drawn from evidence. We must therefore consider the rulings, then the proofs and their classes, then the means of drawing rulings from them, and finally the qualities of the person entitled to draw them.
records.body: “Draw from” tracks iqtibās, which leads into the sustained fruit-and-harvest image. It does not posit an extra, independent source of law.

records.title: Fruit, productive source, method, and harvester
records.ar: فإن الأحكام ثمرات وكل ثمرة فلها صفة وحقيقة في نفسها ولها مثمر ومستثمر وطريق في الاستثمار، والثمرة هي الأحكام أعني الوجوب والحظر والندب والكراهة والإباحة والحسن والقبح والقضاء والأداء والصحة والفساد وغيرها والمثمر هي الأدلة وهي ثلاثة الكتاب والسنة والإجماع فقط.
records.en: Legal rulings are fruits. Every fruit has a character and reality of its own, something that brings it forth, someone who harvests it, and a way of harvesting it. The fruits are the rulings—obligation, prohibition, recommendation, disapproval, permission, goodness and badness, performance and restitution, validity and invalidity, and the rest. The things that bear fruit are the proofs, which are three: the Book, the Sunna, and consensus.
records.body: The distinction between what counts as evidence and the method of drawing from evidence becomes the organizing device for this entire book.

records.title: The four modes of indication
records.ar: وطرق الاستثمار هي وجوه دلالة الأدلة وهي أربعة، إذ الأقوال إما أن تدل على الشيء بصيغتها ومنظومها أو بفحواها ومفهومها وباقتضائها وضرورتها أو بمعقولها ومعناها المستنبط منها.
records.en: The methods of harvesting are the modes in which proofs indicate their conclusions. These are four: an utterance may indicate something by its articulated form and explicit wording; by its import and understood sense; by what its necessary implications require; or by its intelligible meaning as drawn from it.
records.body: The pairing and counting require attention to al-Ghazālī’s own subsequent articulation, not a one-to-one equation with modern literal, contextual, or purposive methods. Hammad foregrounds the explicit, implicit and rationally entailed types of indication. The new version keeps the metaphor of extracting the fruit and preserves the distinction between the utterance’s form, its purport, what it necessarily implies, and the inference that joins premises. The terms require continued mapping to his later chapters on dalāla.

records.title: The jurist and the four axes
records.ar: والمستثمر هو المجتهد ولا بد من معرفة صفاته وشروطه وأحكامه، فإذا جملة الأصول تدور على أربعة أقطاب: القطب الأول في الأحكام والبداءة بها أولى لأنها الثمرة المطلوبة. القطب الثاني في الأدلة وهي الكتاب والسنة والإجماع. القطب الثالث في طريق الاستثمار وهو وجوه دلالة الأدلة. القطب الرابع في المستثمر وهو المجتهد الذي يحكم بظنه، ويقابله المقلد الذي يلزمه اتباعه.
records.en: The harvester is the mujtahid; his qualifications, conditions, and rulings must therefore be known. The entire discipline revolves around four principal axes: first, the rulings, with which we begin because they are the fruits sought; second, the proofs—the Book, the Sunna, and consensus; third, the process of harvesting, namely the modes through which proofs indicate; and fourth, the harvester himself, the mujtahid, who renders judgment on the basis of his considered probability, opposite whom stands the follower who is bound to follow him.
records.body: The jurist “judges by his ẓann” is al-Ghazālī’s phrase at the overview, well before the long debate over divergent ijtihād. Ẓann is not merely an exceptional failure of proof.

records.title: Interpretation has several routes
records.ar: وطرق الاستثمار هي وجوه دلالة الأدلة وهي أربعة
records.en: The methods of drawing out legal rulings are the modes in which the proofs signify, and these modes are four.
records.body: “Drawing out” retains the author’s sustained imagery of the fruit, its producer, the cultivator, and the manner of harvesting.

records.title: The inquirer and the follower
records.ar: القطب الرابع في المستثمر وهو المجتهد الذي يحكم بظنه، ويقابله المقلد الذي يلزمه اتباعه
records.en: The fourth principal division concerns the one who draws out the fruit: the mujtahid, who reaches a ruling through predominant judgment. Opposite him stands the follower, whose task is to follow that jurist.
records.body: This fourth place is essential for connecting the results of probable argument to the qualified practitioner authorized to act on them.

records.title: Rules as legal addresses, not properties of acts
records.ar: فيتبين أنه عبارة عن خطاب الشرع وليس وصفا للفعل ولا حسن ولا قبح ولا مدخل للعقل فيه ولا حكم قبل ورود الشرع
records.en: The ruling is shown to be an address of revealed law, not an intrinsic description of the act—not simply its being good or bad. On this account reason does not itself establish such a legal ruling before the revealed address arrives.
records.body: Here al-Ghazālī outlines an Ashʿarī legal-theological argument; it should not be flattened into the claim that actions have no intelligible natural features.

records.title: Why the definitions of knowledge and evidence arose
records.ar: اعلم أنه لما رجع حد أصول الفقه إلى معرفة أدلة الأحكام اشتمل الحد على ثلاثة ألفاظ: المعرفة والدليل والحكم، فقالوا: إذا لم يكن بد من معرفة الحكم حتى كان معرفته أحد الأقطاب الأربعة فلا بد أيضا من معرفة الدليل ومعرفة المعرفة، أعني العلم.
records.en: Know that once the definition of uṣūl al-fiqh had been reduced to knowing the proofs of rulings, it comprised three terms: knowing, proof, and ruling. Scholars therefore said: if knowledge of a ruling is indispensable—so indispensable that it constitutes one of the four principal divisions—then it is equally necessary to know what a proof is and what knowing itself means, that is, to investigate knowledge.
records.body: Al-Ghazālī is reporting the development of a curriculum from terms contained in its definition, not conceding that a full epistemology belongs intrinsically to uṣūl.

records.title: The danger of importing another discipline wholesale
records.ar: وذلك مجاوزة لحد هذا العلم وخلط له بالكلام، وإنما أكثر فيه المتكلمون من الأصوليين لغلبة الكلام على طبائعهم فحملهم حب صناعتهم على خلطه بهذه الصنعة، كما حمل حب اللغة والنحو بعض الأصوليين على مزج جملة من النحو بالأصول.
records.en: This exceeds the proper bounds of the discipline and mixes it with theology. The theologians among the uṣūlīs expanded it in that direction because theological debate had come to dominate their intellectual habits: love of their own craft led them to mix it with this one, just as attachment to language and grammar led some uṣūlīs to import a considerable quantity of grammar into legal theory.
records.body: The author does not simply reject rational method. He distinguishes supplying concepts needed by an inquiry from pursuing external disputes within its pages.

records.title: The limit of legitimate prolegomena
records.ar: وأما معرفة حجية الإجماع وحجية القياس فذلك من خاصية أصول الفقه، فذكر حجية العلم والنظر على منكريه استجرار الأصول إلى الفروع.
records.en: Establishing the probative authority of consensus and of analogy is a task proper to uṣūl al-fiqh. By contrast, arguing for the authority of knowledge and reasoning against those who deny them drags the science of principles into subjects that are not its own.
records.body: This passage helps distinguish legal evidentiary authority from general epistemic justification, and matters for comparisons with Aristotelian demonstrative method.

records.title: The proper boundary of legal theory
records.ar: وأما معرفة حجية الإجماع وحجية القياس فذلك من خاصية أصول الفقه
records.en: But determining the probative authority of consensus and of analogy belongs specifically to the principles of jurisprudence.
records.body: Ḥujjiyya is the status of furnishing an authoritative ground for inference, not simply whether consensus or analogy exists. Al-Ghazālī distinguishes that question from general epistemology.

records.title: Single concepts cannot yet be true or false
records.ar: وأما الأول فيستحيل فيه التصديق والتكذيب إذ لا يتطرق التصديق إلا إلى خبر، وأقل ما يتركب منه جزءان مفردان وصف وموصوف، فإذا نسب الوصف إلى الموصوف بنفي أو إثبات صدق أو كذب.
records.en: The first kind cannot admit assent or rejection as true or false, because such assessment is possible only with a proposition. At the least, a proposition is composed of two single elements, something described and a description. Only when the description is predicated of the subject, affirmatively or negatively, can the resulting statement be true or false.
records.body: The minimal structure here is logical predication. It should not be confused with a legal judgement (ḥukm sharʿī), whose validity involves the authority of the revealed address.

records.title: Every assent presupposes conceptual grasp
records.ar: وكل علم تطرق إليه تصديق فمن ضرورته أن يتقدم عليه معرفتان أي تصوران، فإن من لا يعرف المفرد كيف يعلم المركب، ومن لا يفهم معنى العالم ومعنى الحادث كيف يعلم أن العالم حادث.
records.en: Every cognition that admits assent must necessarily be preceded by two acts of acquaintance—two conceptions. For how could someone know a compound proposition who does not grasp its component notions? How could one know that the world is originated without first understanding what “world” and “originated” mean?
records.body: The sequence and examples are closely paralleled in Ghazālī’s logical manual. This supports a direct comparative text, not a generic equation of law and demonstration.

records.title: Primary and sought concepts
records.ar: ومعرفة المفردات قسمان: أولي وهو الذي لا يطلب بالبحث وهو الذي يرتسم معناه في النفس من غير بحث وطلب كلفظ الوجود والشيء وككثير من المحسوسات، ومطلوب وهو الذي يدل اسمه منه على أمر جملي غير مفصل ولا مفسر فيطلب تفسيره بالحد، وكذلك العلم ينقسم إلى أولي كالضروريات وإلى مطلوب كالنظريات.
records.en: Knowledge of individual notions divides in two. Some is primary: its meaning is formed in the mind without investigation, as with “existence,” “thing,” and many sensory objects. Other notions are sought: their names point to something grasped only generally and without articulation, so an account of them is sought by definition. Cognition of propositions is likewise either primary, as in necessary truths, or something to be sought, as in results of theoretical inquiry.
records.body: Al-Ghazālī distinguishes immediately evident intelligibles from contents that require clarification. The contrast underlies his later discussion of what can be demonstrated and what must be presupposed.

records.title: Definition and demonstration have different tasks
records.ar: والمطلوب من المعرفة لا يقتنص إلا بالحد، والمطلوب من العلم الذي يتطرق إليه التصديق والتكذيب لا يقتنص إلا بالبرهان، فالبرهان والحد هو الآلة التي بها يقتنص سائر العلوم المطلوبة.
records.en: What is sought at the level of conceptual acquaintance can be attained only by definition; what is sought in propositional cognition—the kind open to affirmation or denial—can be attained only by demonstration. Thus definition and demonstration are the instruments through which the remaining objects of theoretical knowledge are acquired.
records.body: Definition makes intelligible what a thing is meant to be; demonstration determines whether a propositional claim follows. Later legal evidence may be probabilistic without making every syllogism demonstrative.

records.title: The universal prolegomenon
records.ar: نذكر في هذه المقدمة مدارك العقول وانحصارها في الحد والبرهان، ونذكر شرط الحد الحقيقي وشرط البرهان الحقيقي وأقسامهما على منهاج أوجز مما ذكرناه في كتاب محك النظر وكتاب معيار العلم.
records.en: In this introduction we set out the ways by which intellects apprehend matters, and their delimitation to definition and demonstration. We shall describe the conditions of a genuine definition and a genuine demonstration, together with their varieties, more concisely than we have done in Miḥakk al-Naẓar and Miʿyār al-ʿIlm.
records.body: Both titles appear in the Arabic passage. The link is direct and authorial, not simply topical.

records.title: Why logic is not the exclusive property of uṣūl
records.ar: وليست هذه المقدمة من جملة علم الأصول ولا من مقدماته الخاصة به، بل هي مقدمة العلوم كلها، ومن لا يحيط بها فلا ثقة له بعلومه أصلا، فمن شاء أن لا يكتب هذه المقدمة فليبدأ بالكتاب من القطب الأول.
records.en: This introduction is not part of the science of legal principles, nor is it a preliminary peculiar to it; rather, it is a prolegomenon to all the sciences. Anyone who has not mastered it cannot be trusted in his sciences at all. Whoever wishes to omit this introduction may therefore begin with the first axis of the book.
records.body: The earlier English Volume I translator’s treatment of this introduction requires a direct comparison with the previously uploaded copy; the present edition independently translates the Arabic passage.

records.title: Two kinds of apprehension
records.ar: اعلم أن إدراك الأمور على ضربين: الأول إدراك الذوات المفردة كعلمك بمعنى الجسم والحركة والعالم والحادث والقديم، وسائر ما يدل عليه بالأسامي المفردة. الثاني إدراك نسبة هذه المفردات بعضها إلى بعض بالنفي أو الإثبات.
records.en: Know that apprehension has two kinds. The first is the apprehension of individual notions, such as grasping the meanings of body, motion, the world, the originated, and the eternal, and of other things denoted by single names. The second is apprehending a relation between these notions, whether by affirmation or denial.
records.body: The first kind is associated with conception, the second with assent or judgment. This pair informs the distinction between definition and demonstrative proof. The passage is found within the opening logical introduction. This is an online-text location, not an independently collated manuscript or print-variant reading.

records.title: The knowledge of a single meaning
records.ar: إدراك الذوات المفردة كعلمك بمعنى الجسم والحركة والعالم والحادث والقديم
records.en: The first sort of apprehension concerns single things or meanings: for example, one grasps what body, movement, world, originated, and eternal signify.
records.body: It should not simply be translated “simple substance”; this is an intentional/logical distinction.

records.title: The knowledge of an affirmative or negative relation
records.ar: الثاني: إدراك نسبة هذه المفردات بعضها إلى بعض بالنفي أو الإثبات
records.en: The second sort of apprehension consists in grasping a relation among these units by affirming or denying one of another.
records.body: The structure of this passage closely reproduces the treatment of singular terms and propositions in al-Ghazālī’s earlier logical manual.

records.title: Truth or falsity requires predication
records.ar: والضرب الأخير هو الذي يتطرق إليه التصديق والتكذيب، وأما الأول فيستحيل فيه التصديق والتكذيب
records.en: It is this latter sort of apprehension that admits assent or denial. The first sort, considered by itself, cannot be affirmed as true or rejected as false.
records.body: The first distinction is between concepts and propositions, whereas the subsequent distinction of yaqīn and ẓann concerns degrees or kinds of assent to propositions.

records.title: Conception and assent
records.ar: وقد سمى المنطقيون معرفة المفردات تصورا ومعرفة النسبة الخبرية بينهما تصديقا فقالوا: العلم إما تصور وإما تصديق
records.en: The logicians call grasping the single terms *conception* (taṣawwur), and apprehending their asserted relation *assent* (taṣdīq). In their terminology cognition is thus either conception or assent.
records.body: This is not a division between literal and metaphorical knowledge, nor between religious assent and scientific conception.

records.title: The two instruments of inquiry
records.ar: والمطلوب من المعرفة لا يقتنص إلا بالحد، والمطلوب من العلم الذي يتطرق إليه التصديق والتكذيب لا يقتنص إلا بالبرهان
records.en: A concept whose meaning must be sought is captured through a definition; a proposition to which truth and falsehood apply is established through demonstration.
records.body: The exposition in Miḥakk al-Naẓar closely matches both the division and its pairing with definition and demonstration.

records.title: What is prior and what is sought
records.ar: ومعرفة المفردات قسمان: أولي وهو الذي لا يطلب بالبحث؛ ومطلوب وهو الذي يدل اسمه منه على أمر جملي غير مفصل
records.en: Conception of individual meanings is of two kinds. One is primary and does not need to be sought by investigation; the other begins from a general, unarticulated grasp and requires the meaning to be made explicit.
records.body: Primary is not “chronologically first” in every individual’s history; it marks what is not established through another definition.

records.title: Demonstration depends on the premises
records.ar: والاعتقاد الجزم ينحصر في سبعة أقسام: الأول الأوليات
records.en: Grounds of firm assent fall into seven classes. The first consists of primary truths grasped immediately by the intellect.
records.body: A formally valid syllogism does not by itself ensure demonstrated certainty; the status of its premises must also be established.

records.title: The law of contradiction as a primary truth
records.ar: مثل علم الإنسان بوجود نفسه وبأن الواحد لا يكون قديما حادثا وأن النقيضين إذا صدق أحدهما كذب الآخر
records.en: Examples include a person’s awareness of his own existence, the impossibility of one thing being both eternal and originated, and the impossibility of both contradictories being true.
records.body: Keep the contrast between contraries and contradictories distinct where al-Ghazālī does; this short excerpt specifically names contradiction.

records.title: What demonstration consists in
records.ar: والبرهان عبارة عن مقدمتين معلومتين تؤلف تأليفا مخصوصا بشرط مخصوص، فيتولد بينهما نتيجة
records.en: Demonstration consists in two known premises combined in a determinate arrangement, subject to a determinate condition, from which a conclusion follows.
records.body: This describes the formal configuration of an inference; the degree of certainty delivered also depends on the epistemic standing of its premises, treated separately in the material of demonstration.

records.title: Demonstrative, dialectical, and juristic premises
records.ar: فإن كانت المقدمات قطعية سميناها برهانا وإن كانت مسلمة سميناها قياسا جدليا وإن كانت مظنونة سميناها قياسا فقهيا، وسيأتي الفرق بين اليقين والظن.
records.en: If the premises are conclusive, we call the inference a demonstration; if they are accepted as granted, we call it a dialectical syllogism; and if they are held on probable grounds, we call it a juristic inference. The difference between certainty and probable judgment will be explained later.
records.body: This passage explicitly distinguishes the epistemic force of premises. It limits the sense of burhān as strict proof and uses qiyās across logical and juridical domains. “Demonstration” is strictly tied to certainty of premises in its technical sense. Juristic inference can instead be sound in a practical, defeasible manner.

records.title: A direct reference to Asās al-Qiyās
records.ar: وقد ذكرنا في كتاب أساس القياس أن تسمية هذا قياسا تجوز فإن حاصله راجع إلى ازدواج خصوص تحت عموم.
records.en: We explained in Asās al-Qiyās that calling this “analogy” is a figurative extension: in substance, it consists in joining a particular instance to a general proposition.
records.body: This is a direct authorial link. It is especially valuable for preventing the legal use of qiyās from being flattened into the structure of a syllogism or vice versa.

records.title: The ruling is a divine legal address
records.ar: أما التمهيد فهو أن الحكم عندنا عبارة عن خطاب الشرع إذا تعلق بأفعال المكلفين
records.en: As a preliminary, what we call a legal ruling is the address of the revealed Law insofar as it concerns the acts of those answerable to it.
records.body: What is ontologically primary is the authoritative address; the predicates “obligatory” and “prohibited” qualify acts in relation to this address.

records.title: Three elementary responses
records.ar: فالحرام هو المقول فيه اتركوه ولا تفعلوه، والواجب هو المقول فيه افعلوه ولا تتركوه
records.en: What is prohibited is that concerning which the address says “Leave it; do not do it.” What is obligatory is that concerning which it says “Do it; do not leave it.”
records.body: The imperatives are illustrations of the force of the address, not a claim that every command or prohibition appears in precisely this verbal formula.

records.title: Optional choice is also expressed by address
records.ar: والمباح هو المقول فيه إن شئتم فافعلوه وإن شئتم فاتركوه
records.en: What is permitted is that of which it is said, “If you wish, do it; and if you wish, leave it.”
records.body: A later discussion distinguishes a permissive legal address from the mere absence of a legal pronouncement.

records.title: Why original permissibility is not a prior enacted permission
records.ar: المباح يستدعي مبيحا كما يستدعي العلم والذكر ذاكرا وعالما
records.en: Permissibility presupposes one who permits, just as knowing and remembering presuppose a knower and one who remembers.
records.body: Al-Ghazālī’s distinction concerns whether a normative address has occurred; he can still admit the absence of liability without calling it a prior legal dispensation.

records.title: The five evaluative categories
records.ar: أقسام الأحكام الثابتة لأفعال المكلفين خمسة: الواجب والمحظور والمباح والمندوب والمكروه
records.en: There are five classes of legal rulings concerning the acts of accountable persons: obligatory, prohibited, permitted, recommended, and reprehensible.
records.body: The obligatory and recommended are not interchangeable, nor do prohibited and reprehensible have the same practical force.

records.title: Obligation and recommendation distinguished
records.ar: فإن ورد باقتضاء الفعل فهو أمر فإما أن يقترن به الإشعار بعقاب على الترك فيكون واجبا أو لا يقترن فيكون ندبا
records.en: When the address demands the performance of an act, it is a command. If it carries notice of punishment for omission, the act is obligatory; if not, it is recommended.
records.body: The category depends upon the demand together with its legal consequence, not merely the occurrence of an imperative grammatical form.

records.title: Ruling and the divine address
records.ar: أما نفس الحكم فقد ذكرناه وأنه يرجع إلى الخطاب
records.en: As for the ruling itself, we have already explained that it is reducible to an address.
records.body: Khaṭāb should not automatically be glossed as an enacted statute or a subjective quality of the act. It refers here to the Lawgiver’s communicative address within al-Ghazālī’s theory of obligation. The governing discussion occupies a larger unit than this opening phrase; the present reader does not claim that the whole account has been translated.

records.title: Consensus as an object of proof
records.ar: ومن حاول إثبات كون الإجماع حجة افتقر إلى تفهيم لفظ الإجماع أولا وبيان تصوره ثانيا
records.en: Whoever seeks to establish consensus as an authoritative proof must first explain the term and what is conceived by it.
records.body: He explicitly distinguishes conceptual determination from the separate attempt to prove its authority. This reprises the logical introduction.

records.title: The meaning of consensus
records.ar: فإنما نعني به اتفاق أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم خاصة على أمر من الأمور الدينية
records.en: By consensus here we mean specifically the agreement of Muḥammad’s community upon a matter of religion.
records.body: The later discussion asks who counts in constituting the consensus and what form of agreement must be made evident.

records.title: Silence is not spoken agreement
records.ar: وتمام النظر في هذا الركن ببيان أن السكوت ليس كالنطق وأن انقراض العصر ليس بشرط
records.en: A full treatment of this constituent requires showing that silence is not the equivalent of an expressed opinion, and that the passing away of an entire generation is not a condition.
records.body: Not every failure to object constitutes a binding agreement. He separately analyses testimony, timing, and mode of expression.

records.title: Three positions of legal interest relative to the sources
records.ar: القسم الثالث: ما لم يشهد له من الشرع بالبطلان ولا بالاعتبار نص معين وهذا في محل النظر
records.en: The third class comprises considerations for which no particular revealed text attests either rejection or acceptance. This is the very point that requires investigation.
records.body: Neither the existence of apparent benefit nor its absence from a particular text settles the question of probative legitimacy.

records.title: Why an expedient preference cannot override text
records.ar: فكانت المصلحة في إيجاب الصوم لينزجر به، فهذا قول باطل ومخالف لنص الكتاب بالمصلحة
records.en: It was claimed that requiring fasting would restrain the offender more effectively; but that judgment is unsound when it sets an alleged interest against the express text.
records.body: The quoted argument is a counterexample rejected by al-Ghazālī; the new translation distinguishes interlocutor claims from the author’s conclusion.

records.title: Why maṣlaḥa cannot be an autonomous fifth source
records.ar: إذ من ظن أنه أصل خامس فقد أخطأ؛ لأنا رددنا المصلحة إلى حفظ مقاصد الشرع
records.en: To suppose that interest constitutes a fifth foundational source is an error, since we have referred legally relevant interest back to preserving the purposes of the revealed Law.
records.body: The point is about independent evidentiary authority, not a claim that preservation of the law’s purposes is unimportant.

records.title: Where the law’s purposes are known
records.ar: ومقاصد الشرع تعرف بالكتاب والسنة والإجماع
records.en: The purposes of the revealed Law are known through the Book, the Sunna, and consensus.
records.body: An assertion of an attractive end does not automatically establish that end as an authorized legal purpose.

records.title: Ordinary advantage is not the technical criterion
records.ar: أما المصلحة فهي عبارة في الأصل عن جلب منفعة أو دفع مضرة، ولسنا نعني به ذلك، فإن جلب المنفعة ودفع المضرة مقاصد الخلق وصلاح الخلق في تحصيل مقاصدهم، لكنا نعني بالمصلحة المحافظة على مقصود الشرع.
records.en: In its original sense, maṣlaḥa is bringing about an advantage or warding off a harm. That, however, is not what we intend here. Acquiring advantage and avoiding harm are the aims of human beings, and their well-being consists in attaining the ends they seek. By maṣlaḥa we instead mean preserving what the revealed Law intends.
records.body: This is not a simple identification of benefits with subjective preference. He specifies a juridically authoritative criterion related to the Lawgiver’s ends.

records.title: The five protected fundamentals
records.ar: ومقصود الشرع من الخلق خمسة: وهو أن يحفظ عليهم دينهم ونفسهم وعقلهم ونسلهم ومالهم، فكل ما يتضمن حفظ هذه الأصول الخمسة فهو مصلحة، وكل ما يفوت هذه الأصول فهو مفسدة ودفعها مصلحة.
records.en: The purposes of the Law concerning human beings are five: to preserve for them religion, life, intellect, lineage, and property. Whatever secures these five fundamentals is a legal interest (maṣlaḥa); whatever undermines them is a corruption or harm (mafsada), and preventing that harm is itself a legal interest.
records.body: This is a criterion within the demonstration of admissible interests; in the later passage Ghazālī resists constructing an independent fifth source from unrestricted assessments of benefit.

records.title: Common benefit and technical maṣlaḥa
records.ar: أما المصلحة فهي عبارة في الأصل عن جلب منفعة أو دفع مضرة، ولسنا نعني به ذلك، فإن جلب المنفعة ودفع المضرة مقاصد الخلق وصلاح الخلق في تحصيل مقاصدهم.
records.en: In its primary usage, maṣlaḥa means securing a benefit or averting a harm. But this is not what we intend by it here. For securing benefits and averting harms are people’s own aims, and their welfare consists in attaining what they seek.
records.body: Al-Ghazālī explicitly sets aside the common human-benefit meaning before defining the narrower legal-technical sense. The contrast is fundamental to any comparison with later utilitarian or Thomist accounts of the common good.

records.title: The five protected fundamentals
records.ar: لكنا نعني بالمصلحة المحافظة على مقصود الشرع، ومقصود الشرع من الخلق خمسة: وهو أن يحفظ عليهم دينهم ونفسهم وعقلهم ونسلهم ومالهم. فكل ما يتضمن حفظ هذه الأصول الخمسة فهو مصلحة، وكل ما يفوت هذه الأصول فهو مفسدة ودفعها مصلحة.
records.en: What we mean by maṣlaḥa, however, is safeguarding the purpose of the revealed Law. The Law’s purposes for human beings are five: that their religion, life, intellect, progeny, and property be safeguarded. Whatever protects these five fundamentals is a maṣlaḥa; whatever undermines them is a mafsada, a harm or corruption; and averting such corruption is itself a maṣlaḥa.
records.body: Neither the five ends nor the mere presence of benefit automatically gives a particular act a valid ʿilla. Al-Ghazālī’s argument about the relevance and ranking of interests continues beyond this excerpt. In Shifāʾ al-Ghalīl, he asks what makes a meaning legally suitable and speaks of meanings pointing toward the aspects and signs of interests. This comparison is grounded in a distinct primary passage, not presented as a quotation from al-Mustaṣfā.

records.title: The three ranks of interests
records.ar: المصلحة باعتبار قوتها في ذاتها تنقسم إلى ما هي في رتبة الضرورات وإلى ما هي في رتبة الحاجات وإلى ما يتعلق بالتحسينات والتزيينات
records.en: Considered according to their intrinsic weight, interests are divided into necessities, needs, and those pertaining to refinement and adornment.
records.body: Darūrāt / ḥājāt / taḥsīnāt is a grading of legal interests or ends, not a typology of persons or castes.

records.title: The five fundamentals and deprivation
records.ar: فكل ما يتضمن حفظ هذه الأصول الخمسة فهو مصلحة وكل ما يفوت هذه الأصول فهو مفسدة ودفعها مصلحة
records.en: Whatever sustains these five foundational objects is an interest; whatever defeats them is a corruption, and preventing that corruption is also an interest.
records.body: Notice the two directions of legal concern: maintaining the fundamental good and preventing an injury to it.

records.title: Conflicts require prioritization
records.ar: وحيث ذكرنا خلافا فذلك عند تعارض مصلحتين ومقصودين، وعند ذلك ترجيح الأقوى
records.en: Where we have spoken of disagreement, it concerns conflict between two interests or two purposes; in that event, the stronger claim must receive priority.
records.body: Strength is adjudicated within the system of law’s recognized ends and proofs, not by an unregulated modern cost-benefit calculation.

records.title: Why maṣlaḥa is not an independent fifth source
records.ar: إذ من ظن أنه أصل خامس فقد أخطأ؛ لأنا رددنا المصلحة إلى حفظ مقاصد الشرع، ومقاصد الشرع تعرف بالكتاب والسنة والإجماع. فكل مصلحة لا ترجع إلى حفظ مقصود فهم من الكتاب والسنة والإجماع وكانت من المصالح الغريبة التي لا تلائم تصرفات الشرع فهي باطلة مطرحة.
records.en: Anyone who supposes it to be a fifth independent source is mistaken. We have reduced maṣlaḥa to the preservation of the Law’s purposes; and those purposes are known from the Book, the Sunna, and consensus. Consequently, an alleged interest that cannot be referred back to a purpose understood from those sources, but instead stands alien to the Law’s established manner of acting, is rejected as invalid.
records.body: The status of an unenumerated interest must be proved through its affinity with juridically established ends; the term does not license free-standing judicial legislation.

records.title: The operative definition of juristic analogy
records.ar: وحده أنه حمل معلوم على معلوم في إثبات حكم لهما أو نفيه عنهما بأمر جامع بينهما من إثبات حكم أو صفة أو نفيهما عنهما.
records.en: Its definition is to carry what is known of one case over to another known case, in affirming or negating a ruling in respect of the two, by virtue of a feature that joins them, whether that commonality is the affirmation or negation of a ruling or of a characteristic.
records.body: This is a definition of relating cases through a shared factor. Compare the quite different definition of a syllogism in Miḥakk; the same Arabic word can name different intellectual operations.

records.title: Not every association warrants analogical transfer
records.ar: ثم إن كان الجامع موجبا للاجتماع على الحكم كان قياسا صحيحا وإلا كان فاسدا، واسم القياس يشتمل على الصحيح والفاسد في اللغة.
records.en: If the shared element actually warrants the cases being joined in their ruling, the analogy is sound; otherwise it is defective. In ordinary usage, the word “analogy” can apply to both sound and unsound forms.
records.body: Being able to name a feature common to two cases is not sufficient; the relation to the legal ruling must be warranted rather than merely imagined.

records.title: The four indispensable members of an analogy
records.ar: ولا بد في كل قياس من فرع وأصل وعلة وحكم، وليس من شرط الفرع والأصل كونهما موجودين بل ربما يستدل بالنفي على النفي.
records.en: Every analogy requires a new case (farʿ), an original case (aṣl), a legal ground (ʿilla), and a ruling (ḥukm). It is not a condition of the new case or the original that the object actually exists: one may sometimes infer one negation from another.
records.body: The legal ground is a function in a juridical inference. It need not signify an efficient cause in natural philosophy or the full wisdom behind legislation.

records.title: Four grades of analogical reasoning
records.ar: وبيانه أن القياس أربعة أنواع: المؤثر ثم المناسب ثم الشبه ثم الطرد
records.en: The explanation is that analogical inference has four kinds: the demonstrably effective, the suitably related, the resembling, and bare concomitance.
