records.body: Do not make the four kinds equally probative. Al-Ghazālī orders them by how securely the attribute is tied to rulings recognized by law.

records.title: The higher end of the spectrum
records.ar: وأدناها الطرد الذي ينبغي أن ينكره كل قائل بالقياس وأعلاها ما في معنى الأصل
records.en: At the weakest extreme lies mere regular concomitance, which even proponents of analogy ought to reject; at the strongest stands a case included in the meaning of the original.
records.body: Al-Ghazālī argues against mechanically extending the law on the basis of attributes that lack a plausible evidentiary connection to the rule.

records.title: Recognizing effective legal attributes
records.ar: والمؤثر يعرف كونه مؤثرا بنص أو إجماع أو سبر حاصر
records.en: An attribute is established as legally effective through an explicit text, consensus, or an exhaustive process of elimination among the possible candidates.
records.body: Here it denotes exhaustive consideration and elimination, not ordinary observation or statistical survey alone.

records.title: Analogy generates different degrees of probability
records.ar: فلأجل ذلك تتفاوت درجات الظن والأعلى مقدم على الأسفل والأقرب مقدم على الأبعد في الجنسية
records.en: Accordingly, probable judgments admit different degrees: the stronger takes precedence over the weaker, and what belongs to a more closely related kind over what belongs to a more remote one.
records.body: This is a central bridge from logical gradation to juristic choice, without pretending that such premises yield apodictic necessity.

records.title: Three arts of the final division
records.ar: ويشتمل هذا القطب على ثلاثة فنون: فن في الاجتهاد، وفن في التقليد، وفن في ترجيح المجتهد دليلا على دليل عند التعارض.
records.en: This principal division comprises three arts: one investigating juristic effort (ijtihād), another following an authority (taqlīd), and a third the jurist’s preference of one proof over another when they conflict.
records.body: Al-Ghazālī does not equate every legally relevant act of knowledge with ijtihād. A lay follower and a qualified inquirer have different relations to the proof.

records.title: Exertion must involve real difficulty
records.ar: وهو عبارة عن بذل المجهود واستفراغ الوسع في فعل من الأفعال، ولا يستعمل إلا فيما فيه كلفة وجهد، فيقال: اجتهد في حمل حجر الرحا، ولا يقال: اجتهد في حمل خردلة.
records.en: In its ordinary sense, ijtihād is to expend one’s utmost effort and exhaust one’s capacity in an action. The word is used only where the task entails genuine difficulty and exertion: one says that someone strove to lift a millstone, but not that he strove to lift a mustard seed.
records.body: The millstone/mustard-seed contrast explains the verbal sense of exertion, not an independent legal criterion of great bodily hardship.

records.title: The full technical definition of juristic effort
records.ar: لكن صار اللفظ في عرف العلماء مخصوصا ببذل المجتهد وسعه في طلب العلم بأحكام الشريعة، والاجتهاد التام أن يبذل الوسع في الطلب بحيث يحس من نفسه بالعجز عن مزيد طلب.
records.en: In the scholars’ technical usage, the expression has become specific to the qualified jurist’s expenditure of his capacity in seeking knowledge of the Law’s rulings. Fully accomplished ijtihād consists in pursuing the inquiry to the point where the inquirer recognizes that no further search lies within his capacity.
records.body: Completion describes exhaustive inquiry by a qualified subject, not a claim that every conclusion thereby becomes a necessary demonstration.

records.title: The first qualification: mastery of legal evidence
records.ar: أحدهما أن يكون محيطا بمدارك الشرع متمكنا من استثارة الظن بالنظر فيها وتقديم ما يجب تقديمه وتأخير ما يجب تأخيره.
records.en: The first condition is that the jurist encompass the avenues by which the Law is known, possess the capacity to elicit a preponderant conclusion by examining them, and know how to give priority to what deserves priority and defer what should come later.
records.body: The ability to elicit ẓann by ordered consideration of proofs is a positive qualification. It does not equate conjecture with arbitrary opinion.

records.title: The second qualification: whose fatwā may be relied upon
records.ar: الثاني: أن يكون عدلا مجتنبا للمعاصي القادحة في العدالة، وهذا يشترط لجواز الاعتماد على فتواه فمن ليس عدلا فلا تقبل فتواه، أما هو في نفسه فلا، فكأن العدالة شرط القبول للفتوى لا شرط صحة الاجتهاد.
records.en: The second is that the jurist be upright, avoiding sins that compromise probity. This is required for others to be entitled to rely upon his fatwā: the fatwā of someone without such uprightness is not accepted. That restriction does not apply to the jurist’s reasoning as it concerns him personally. Uprightness is thus a condition of the fatwā’s acceptance, rather than a condition of the validity of the act of ijtihād.
records.body: A requirement governing public reliance on a fatwā must not be silently transformed into a defect of every intellectual operation of a morally compromised scholar.

records.title: The proper subject of juristic effort
records.ar: والمجتهد فيه كل حكم شرعي ليس فيه دليل قطعي، واحترزنا بالشرعي عن العقليات ومسائل الكلام، فإن الحق فيها واحد والمصيب واحد والمخطئ آثم.
records.en: The proper subject of ijtihād is every legal ruling for which no decisive proof is available. The qualification “legal” excludes questions of rational demonstration and theology: in those domains, according to this argument, the truth is one, and there is one who has it right, while the person in error is blameworthy.
records.body: The claim concerns an epistemic/legal domain. It must be read alongside the following distinction concerning obvious obligations established by decisive proofs.

records.title: Subject matter of juristic inquiry
records.ar: والمجتهد فيه كل حكم شرعي ليس فيه دليل قطعي
records.en: A question open to qualified juristic inquiry is any legal ruling for which no decisive proof is available.
records.body: The legal question remains open to inquiry because its evidence is not demonstratively conclusive, not merely because jurists happen to disagree.

records.title: Reasoned error and conclusive proof
records.ar: ووجوب الصلوات الخمس والزكوات وما اتفقت عليه الأمة من جليات الشرع فيها أدلة قطعية
records.en: The obligation of the five prayers, the alms dues, and the manifest principles agreed upon by the community are established by decisive proofs.
records.body: This statement limits the sphere in which disagreement can be excused as an exercise of ijtihād.

records.title: Complete inquiry in its place removes blame
records.ar: والإثم ينتفي عن كل من جمع صفات المجتهدين إذا تمم الاجتهاد في محله، فكل اجتهاد تام إذا صدر من أهله وصادف محله فثمرته حق وصواب، والإثم عن المجتهد منفي.
records.en: Blame is removed from everyone who possesses the qualifications of a mujtahid when he completes his inquiry in the matters to which ijtihād properly applies. Every complete instance of ijtihād undertaken by a competent jurist within its legitimate domain yields an acceptable fruit and a right result, and the jurist incurs no sin for it.
records.body: Al-Ghazālī requires competent agent, complete effort and proper subject matter. The sentence cannot be cited as an unrestricted endorsement of all conflicting opinions.

records.title: An inquiry into predominant probability
records.ar: قلنا: فقد أخطأتم إذ ظننتم أن المجتهد يطلب حكم الله مع علمه بأن حكم الله خطابه، فإن الواقعة لا نص فيها ولا خطاب بل إنما يطلب غلبة الظن.
records.en: We reply: You have erred in supposing that the mujtahid seeks God’s ruling while knowing that God’s ruling is His address. In the case under discussion there is no determinate text and no particular address. What the jurist seeks, rather, is a preponderance of probability.
records.body: This is a passage in the debate on legal correctness and error when no determinate textual ruling is posited. It is not a universal claim that revelation provides no binding rulings. This discussion treats the thesis of taṣwīb (and its opponents) in cases lacking a settled revelatory ruling. It is not a declaration that every legal rule or disagreement is subjectively constituted.

records.title: The sea-crossing analogy
records.ar: وهو كمن كان على ساحل البحر وقيل له: إن غلب على ظنك السلامة أبيح لك الركوب، وإن غلب على ظنك الهلاك حرم عليك الركوب. وقبل حصول الظن لا حكم لله عليك وإنما حكمه يترتب على ظنك ويتبع ظنك بعد حصوله، فهو يطلب الظن دون الإباحة والتحريم.
records.en: He is like someone standing at the shore who is told: “If you predominantly judge the crossing to be safe, you may embark; but if you predominantly judge that it will destroy you, embarking is forbidden.” Before such a judgment is formed, no ruling applies to you on that basis; rather, its application follows the probable judgment once it has arisen. The inquiry thus seeks the judgment of probability, not permission or prohibition themselves.
records.body: The illustration should not be mistaken for legal voluntarism. Its conditional norm is specified, while the jurist’s judgment establishes whether its condition is satisfied.

records.title: Why adjudicated decisions may stand
records.ar: ولو حكم بصحة النكاح حاكم بعد أن خالع الزوج ثلاثا ثم تغير اجتهاده لم يفرق بين الزوجين ولم ينقض اجتهاده السابق بصحة النكاح لمصلحة الحكم، فإنه لو نقض الاجتهاد لنقض النقض أيضا ولتسلسل فاضطربت الأحكام ولم يوثق بها.
records.en: If a judge had already ruled the marriage valid following a triple separation by khulʿ, and subsequently changed his juristic assessment, the couple would not be separated and his earlier decision would not be annulled. This protects the public good of authoritative judgment: if an earlier act of ijtihād could simply be overturned by a later one, the overturning could itself be overturned, producing an endless sequence in which legal decisions become unstable and lose people’s confidence.
records.body: The jurist may change his view without retroactively depriving a completed judicial decision of finality. It is a legal-institutional principle, not a guarantee that the earlier opinion was demonstratively true.

records.title: uṣūl al-fiqh
records.ar: أصول الفقه
records.en: principles of jurisprudence
records.body: The systematic study of the legal rulings’ proofs, their modes of indication, and conditions of qualified legal inference.

records.title: quṭb
records.ar: قطب
records.en: principal division / axis
records.body: One of the four coordinated main divisions in al-Mustaṣfā’s architecture.

records.title: kalām
records.ar: كلام
records.en: dialectical theology
records.body: The discipline that, in this classification, investigates matters most general within religious sciences.

records.title: kullī
records.ar: كلي
records.en: universal
records.body: Treating the most general scope of a field, contrasted here with the more circumscribed objects of particular sciences.

records.title: ḥukm
records.ar: حكم
records.en: legal ruling
records.body: Here, the normative ruling considered in relation to the divine address, as distinguished from an act’s natural property.

records.title: khiṭāb
records.ar: خطاب
records.en: address
records.body: The Lawgiver’s normative address; not automatically a modern legislative statute.

records.title: taklīf
records.ar: تكليف
records.en: moral-legal obligation
records.body: Binding address to accountable persons; its preconditions are discussed within the legal ruling.

records.title: ijmāʿ
records.ar: إجماع
records.en: consensus
records.body: A source claimed to carry normative evidentiary authority; its ḥujjiyya requires argument.

records.title: ḥujjiyya
records.ar: حجية
records.en: probative authority
records.body: The standing of something as an authoritative ground for argument and legal determination.

records.title: qiyās
records.ar: قياس
records.en: analogy / syllogistic inference
records.body: Different domains use qiyās differently: formal syllogism in logic, analogical extension in juristic reasoning.

records.title: ḥadd
records.ar: حد
records.en: definition
records.body: An account identifying what a thing is; treated as a prerequisite for precise theoretical discourse.

records.title: burhān
records.ar: برهان
records.en: demonstration
records.body: An inference formed from premises in a valid configuration; note the distinct certainty or probability of its premises.

records.title: yaqīn
records.ar: يقين
records.en: certainty
records.body: Certain cognition; not to be indiscriminately transferred to all conclusions of juristic ẓann.

records.title: ẓann
records.ar: ظن
records.en: probable judgment
records.body: Defeasible but reasoned assent that may nevertheless furnish an operative juristic basis.

records.title: maṣlaḥa
records.ar: مصلحة
records.en: legally cognizable interest
records.body: For al-Ghazālī here: preservation of the Lawgiver’s purposes, not simple maximization of subjective utility.

records.title: maqāṣid
records.ar: مقاصد
records.en: purposes / ends
records.body: The purposes of the Lawgiver, here concretely articulated by five protected necessities.

records.title: ʿilla
records.ar: علة
records.en: operative reason
records.body: A legal reason or effective basis, not necessarily identical with a broader wisdom or purpose.

records.title: ijtihād
records.ar: اجتهاد
records.en: qualified juristic inquiry
records.body: Exertion of trained juridical capacity in determining rulings under relevant sources and evidence.

records.title: fiqh
records.ar: فقه
records.en: jurisprudence; understanding
records.body: Lexically knowing and understanding; technically knowledge of rulings attaching to the acts of accountable persons.

records.title: dalāla
records.ar: دلالة
records.en: indication / signification
records.body: The relation by which proof or wording signifies a ruling. Its modes are a core part of the third axis.

records.title: taṣawwur
records.ar: تصور
records.en: conception
records.body: The grasp of a single content or meaning without asserting it to be true or false.

records.title: taṣdīq
records.ar: تصديق
records.en: assent / propositional judgment
records.body: Taking an affirmative or negative proposition to be true; epistemic degrees of assent require further distinctions.

records.title: awwaliyyāt
records.ar: أوليات
records.en: first principles
records.body: Judgments known without argumentative mediation, contrasted with truths established through investigation.

records.title: muqaddimāt
records.ar: مقدمات
records.en: premises
records.body: The judgments from which an inference is composed; their strength as premises determines the status of its conclusion.

records.title: mujtahid
records.ar: مجتهد
records.en: qualified juristic inquirer
records.body: A jurist possessing the pertinent interpretative and evidentiary competences to form responsible legal judgments.

records.title: muqallid
records.ar: مقلد
records.en: legal follower
records.body: One who follows a qualified opinion without personally performing the full juristic derivation.

records.title: mubāḥ
records.ar: مباح
records.en: permitted
records.body: A normative option left open by the revealed address; to be distinguished from original nonliability without address.

records.title: wājib
records.ar: واجب
records.en: obligatory
records.body: Demanded performance to which a legal consequence attaches upon deliberate omission.

records.title: mandūb
records.ar: مندوب
records.en: recommended
records.body: An act called for without punishment prescribed for omission.

records.title: mafsada
records.ar: مفسدة
records.en: corruption / injury
records.body: The frustration of a legally recognized interest or purpose; averting it can itself constitute maṣlaḥa.

records.title: istiṣḥāb
records.ar: استصحاب
records.en: presumption of continuity
records.body: Reasoning that the previously established condition remains until an adequate ground of alteration is shown.

records.title: istiṣlāḥ
records.ar: استصلاح
records.en: appeal to legal interest
records.body: Inquiry into a purported maṣlaḥa, whose probative standing requires authorization from the recognized sources and purposes.

records.title: sabab
records.ar: سبب
records.en: occasion / occasioning condition
records.body: That with whose occurrence a ruling is tied, but not therefore identical with a metaphysical efficient cause or the rationale of the rule.

records.title: sharṭ
records.ar: شرط
records.en: legal condition
records.body: A qualification requisite for the application or validity of a ruling, distinguished from its intrinsic cause or object.

records.title: ṣiḥḥa
records.ar: صحة
records.en: legal validity
records.body: The status of an act fulfilling the conditions for juridical effect within a particular doctrinal account.

records.title: fasād
records.ar: فساد
records.en: invalidity / defectiveness
records.body: Failure to satisfy specified juridical requirements; some schools distinguish degrees of legal invalidity.

records.title: rukhṣa
records.ar: رخصة
records.en: concession
records.body: A dispensation in a legally recognized situation of hardship or exception, contrasted with the ordinary rule (ʿazīma).

records.title: ʿazīma
records.ar: عزيمة
records.en: standing rule / resolution
records.body: The ordinary normative force of a duty absent a recognized dispensing condition.

records.title: qaṭʿī
records.ar: قطعي
records.en: decisive / conclusive
records.body: A characterization of evidential decisiveness, distinct from plausible or predominant judgments.

records.title: marātib
records.ar: مراتب
records.en: ranks / degrees
records.body: Orders of priority or epistemic strength; the criteria differ between legal interests and forms of inference.

records.title: ʿadāla
records.ar: عدالة
records.en: uprightness/probity
records.body: A quality relevant to whether another person may rely upon the jurist’s fatwā; not equated by al-Ghazālī with the validity of the jurist’s own reasoning.

records.title: tarjīḥ
records.ar: ترجيح
records.en: reasoned preference
records.body: Evaluating competing proofs and giving precedence to the stronger indication when legally warranted; not arbitrary selection.

records.title: fatwā
records.ar: فتوى
records.en: legal opinion
records.body: A juristic response offered for another person to follow or rely upon; its reception is governed by the standing of the opinion-giver.

records.title: aṣl
records.ar: أصل
records.en: original case / fundamental
records.body: In legal analogy, the original case from which the ruling is extended; in other contexts the term means a principle or source.

records.title: farʿ
records.ar: فرع
records.en: derivative case / branch
records.body: The case newly assessed by analogy; also a subsidiary legal question in the general/particular relation.

records.title: taṣwīb
records.ar: تصويب
records.en: finding a juristic conclusion correct
records.body: The thesis about the status of a duly qualified jurist’s outcome in matters open to ijtihād; requires specifying competent agent and proper subject.

records.title: ʿilm al-bāṭin
records.ar: علم الباطن
records.en: inward science
records.body: Knowledge of the heart and its purification from blameworthy traits, explicitly named in al-Mustaṣfā’s classification of religious disciplines.

records.title: Cross-work source · usul
records.body: Named as longer/more exhaustive than the present work; no line-by-line terminology comparison yet.

records.title: Cross-work source · usul
records.body: Named as briefer than the present work; edition-to-edition conceptual comparison pending.

records.title: Cross-work source · usul
records.body: Named directly; the relation to outward/inward disciplines needs separate passage-level study.

records.title: Cross-work source · usul
records.body: Named directly in the author’s preface.

records.title: Cross-work source · usul
records.body: Named directly in the author’s preface.

records.title: Cross-work source · hadd
records.body: Author directs the reader to an earlier and fuller treatment of definition and demonstration.

records.title: Cross-work source · burhan
records.body: Author explicitly names Miḥakk al-Naẓar for fuller logic.

records.title: Cross-work source · qiyas
records.body: Author explicitly states that his earlier Asās al-Qiyās explained the qualified use of the word qiyās in the example.

records.title: Cross-work source · maslaha
records.ar: المعاني المناسبة: ما تشير إلى وجوه المصالح وأماراتها
records.en: Legally suitable meanings are those that point to the aspects of interests and their indications.
records.body: Compare with the purposes-of-law definition; this Shifāʾ passage emphasizes suitability and indications rather than identifying all legal interests with ordinary benefits.

records.title: Cross-work source · hadd
records.ar: فالمطلوب من المعرفة لا يقتنص إلا بالحد
records.en: The knowledge sought in apprehending a thing is obtained only through definition.
records.body: Miḥakk, introduction: knowledge of a single notion is distinguished from assent to a proposition. Compare the definitional role of ḥadd in the al-Mustaṣfā prolegomenon. Text attested, but print pagination still to be controlled.

records.title: Cross-work source · zann
records.ar: وهذا يسمّى ظناً وله درجات في الميل إلى الزيادة والنقصان لا تحصى
records.en: This is called probable assent (ẓann); its degrees of increase and diminution cannot be numbered.
records.body: Miḥakk, discussion of degrees of assent: ẓann is an inclination toward affirmation compatible with entertaining its opposite, strengthened by testimony and circumstantial evidence. This provides a genuine conceptual parallel, not an identity of legal and logical situations.

records.title: Cross-work source · maqasid
records.ar: وجميع أنواع المناسبات ترجع إلى رعاية المقاصد
records.en: Every kind of legal suitability ultimately concerns the safeguarding of purposes.
records.body: Shifāʾ al-Ghalīl, discussion of the suitable meaning (al-munāsib): the distinction between acquiring a sought good and preserving it against removal supplies context for the objectives-of-law account in al-Mustaṣfā.

records.title: Cross-work source · burhan
records.body: Miḥakk, introduction and discussion of the conditions of syllogism: al-Ghazālī expressly relates sought propositional knowledge to demonstration, distinguishing sound arrangement from the certainty of premises. The relationship is directly checked, but a quotation is deferred pending witness collation.

records.title: Cross-work source · yaqin
records.body: Miḥakk, discussion immediately following the degrees of assent: a syllogism from genuinely certain premises and correctly assembled produces necessary certainty. Useful for understanding the shift from demonstrative yaqīn to juristic ẓann in al-Mustaṣfā.

records.title: Cross-work source · tasawwur
records.ar: فإن العلوم إدراك الذوات المفردة ... وإدراك نسبة هذه المفردات بعضها إلى البعض بالنفي والإثبات
records.en: The sciences involve grasping individual subjects and apprehending their affirmative or negative relations.
records.body: Explicit near-verbatim agreement of the exposition of simple contents and predicative relation; consult the full primary text to inspect wording and local context.

records.title: Cross-work source · hadd
records.ar: فالمطلوب من المعرفة لا يقتنص إلا بالحد والمطلوب من العلم ... لا يقتنص إلا بالحجة والبرهان
records.en: What must be sought in conceptual knowledge is grasped by definition, and propositional knowledge by argument and demonstration.
records.body: High-confidence verbal parallel: the same methodological pairing appears in the logical manual. Al-Mustaṣfā uses the same conception/assent architecture.

records.title: Cross-work source · burhan
records.ar: والخلل يدخل عليه تارة من الأقاويل التي هي مقدمات القياس ... وأخرى من كيفية الترتيب والنظم
records.en: A syllogism can go wrong because of its premises or because of its arrangement and form.
records.body: Directly supports distinguishing the matter and form of reasoning; the legal-theory introduction should not be translated as if all formal inference were automatically certain.

records.title: Cross-work source · tasdiq
records.ar: فإن المعرفة لا تتعدى إلا إلى مفعول واحد والعلم يتعدى إلى مفعولين
records.en: The verb of acquaintance takes one object, whereas the verb of knowing takes two.
records.body: A genuine parallel in al-Mankhūl’s treatment of defining knowledge: the grammatical illustration is reused for the distinction between apprehending a term and assenting to a proposition.

records.title: Cross-work source · usul
records.ar: وأما الأصول فمادته الكلام والفقه واللغة
records.en: The material of uṣūl is theology, fiqh, and language.
records.body: Direct terminological parallel to the scope and sources of the discipline; compare the subsequent distinction between material studied and the final purpose of the science.

records.title: Cross-work source · zann
records.ar: وأخبار الآحاد ومسالك العبر والمقاييس والمستثارة بطرق الاجتهاد ليس من الأصول فإنها مظنونات بجانب أخذها مأخذ القطعيات
records.en: Reports from individuals, paths of inference, analogies and conclusions obtained through ijtihād are not principles in the same strict sense, for they are probable when compared with things accepted as conclusive.
records.body: Shows a stricter epistemic delimitation of the term uṣūl in al-Mankhūl. This should be set against the later systematic treatment of ẓann in al-Mustaṣfā, not interpreted as an absolute rejection of juristic inference.

records.title: Cross-work source · dalala
records.ar: القسم الأول: إن دلالة اللفظ على المعنى ينحصر في ثلاثة أوجه: وهي المطابقة والتضمن والالتزام
records.en: Verbal indication of meaning falls under three aspects: correspondence, inclusion, and entailment.
records.body: Direct logical account of indication; it provides a technical comparator to the legal modes of extracting rulings from verbal evidence.

records.title: Cross-work source · qiyas
records.ar: اعلم أن القياس عبارة عن أقاويل مخصوصة أُلفت تأليفاً مخصوصاً ونُظمت نظماً مخصوصاً بشرط مخصوص يلزم منه رأي هو مطلوب الناظر
records.en: Know that syllogism consists in specified statements compounded and ordered under definite conditions, so that the investigator’s sought conclusion follows.
records.body: The qiyās of logical inference is defined as a structured argument, whereas al-Mustaṣfā I:281 defines juridical analogy through an original case, a new case and their shared ground.

records.title: Cross-work source · kalam
records.ar: وأعني بعلم المعاملة ما يطلب منه مع الكشف العمل به والمقصود من هذا الكتاب علم المعاملة فقط دون علم المكاشفة
records.en: By the science of practice I mean what one seeks in order to act upon it, in addition to discerning it. The concern of this book is the science of practice, not the science of unveiling.
records.body: An authorial parallel concerning the inward discipline named in al-Mustaṣfā I:7. This is a comparison of scopes and aims, not proof that fiqh and inward purification are interchangeable.

records.title: Cross-work source · hadd
records.ar: والمعرفة قسمان: أولى وهو الذي لا يطلب بالبحث كالمفردات المدركة بالحس، ومطلوب وهو الذي يدل اسمه منه على أمر جملي غير مفصل فيطلب تفصيله
records.en: Conceptual acquaintance is of two kinds: primary knowledge not sought by investigation, and that sought when its name indicates a general notion whose detail remains unarticulated.
records.body: Corroborates the division between primary and sought conception, with close verbal parallels in the opening of Miḥakk.

records.title: hadd
records.ar: الحد قول دال على ماهية الشيء
records.en: A definition is a statement that indicates the quiddity of a thing.
records.body: This is a later technical glossary, not al-Ghazālī’s own definition.

records.title: burhan
records.ar: البرهان هو القياس المؤلف من اليقينيات سواء كانت ابتداء وهي الضروريات أو بواسطة وهي النظريات
records.en: Demonstration is a syllogism composed of certainties, whether immediate—those that are necessary—or mediated—those reached through reasoning.
records.body: Use this stricter definition to distinguish al-Ghazālī’s juridical probable premises.

records.title: zann
records.ar: الظن هو الاعتقاد الراجح مع احتمال النقيض، ويستعمل في اليقين والشك
records.en: Ẓann is a predominant conviction with the possibility of its opposite; the word is also used for certainty and for doubt.
records.body: A broader lexical note does not nullify al-Ghazālī’s technical degree of assent.

records.title: illah
records.ar: وشرعا: عبارة عما يجب الحكم به معه
records.en: In legal usage, it designates that with which a ruling must obtain.
records.body: The source distinguishes linguistic, metaphysical and juridical senses; this extracts only the legal definition.

records.title: ijma
records.ar: وفي الاصطلاح: اتفاق المجتهدين في أمة محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام في عصر على أمر ديني
records.en: In technical usage, the agreement of the jurists qualified for independent reasoning within the community of Muḥammad, in a given age, on a religious matter.
records.body: Later term definition; al-Ghazālī’s own qualification of consensus must be read separately.

records.title: ijtihad
records.ar: في اللغة بذل الوسع، وفي الاصطلاح: استفراغ الفقيه الوسع ليحصل له ظن بحكم شرعي
records.en: Lexically, exerting one’s capacity; technically, a jurist’s full exertion of effort so that he may arrive at a probable judgment concerning a legal ruling.
records.body: Provides a useful explicit link between effort and the epistemic status of the conclusion.

records.title: zann
records.ar: الظن شك ويقين إلا أنه ليس بيقين عيان إنما هو يقين تدبر
records.en: Ẓann can designate doubt or certainty, though the latter is not the certainty of direct seeing but of reflective consideration.
records.body: A wider range than juristic predominant probability: do not substitute this lexical range wholesale for the author’s technical argument.

records.title: hukm
records.ar: الله سبحانه وتعالى أحكم الحاكمين، وهو الحكيم له الحكم
records.en: God, exalted, is the most just of judges; He is the Wise, and judgment belongs to Him.
records.body: The passage concerns divine judgment in lexical and religious usage, not the precise uṣūl definition of ruling as address.

records.title: illah
records.ar: عِلَّة
records.en: Cause, reason, motive; also illness, defect, excuse or pretext, according to context.
records.body: A broader Arabic lexical family. The legal operative ʿilla must be determined from the juristic passage; the “illness” sense does not define the technical cause.

records.title: tasawwur
records.ar: إدراك الذوات المفردة
records.en: The apprehension of single contents or meanings.
records.body: Included separately from later lexica because it is significantly stronger evidence for al-Ghazālī’s own use of the concept.

records.title: tasdiq
records.ar: إدراك نسبة هذه المفردات بعضها إلى البعض بالنفي والإثبات
records.en: To apprehend an affirmative or negative relation between individual meanings.
records.body: Conceptual links to the author’s logic work are not retroactively ascribed to Ibn Manẓūr or al-Jurjānī.

records.title: zann
records.ar: الظن هو الاعتقاد الراجح مع احتمال النقيض ويستعمل في اليقين والشك
records.en: Ẓann is a preponderant belief that retains the possibility of its contrary; the term is also used for certainty and for doubt.
records.body: This later definition distinguishes preponderance from both logically conclusive knowledge and equipollent doubt.

records.title: qiyas
records.ar: قول مؤلف من قضايا إذا سلمت لزم عنها لذاتها قول آخر
records.en: In logic: a discourse composed of propositions which, once granted, necessitate another proposition through themselves.
records.body: This defines the logicians’ qiyās and is not a definition of legal analogical transfer.

records.title: qiyas
records.ar: وعند أهل الأصول: القياس: إبانة مثل حكم المذكورين بمثل علته في الآخر
records.en: Among scholars of legal theory: qiyās manifests a ruling like that of a named case in another case by reason of a corresponding legal ground.
records.body: Later technical contrast to the logical sense, useful for the user’s Aristotelian comparison.

records.title: yaqin
records.ar: اليقين: العلم وإزاحة الشك وتحقيق الأمر
records.en: Yaqīn is knowledge, the removal of doubt, and the ascertainment of a matter.
records.body: The lexical sense is broader than the rigorous conditions of demonstrative certainty discussed by al-Ghazālī.

records.title: zann
records.ar: ثم إطلاق الظن على الاعتقاد الراجح هو المشهور
records.en: The standard use of the term ẓann is for a belief in which one side predominates.
records.body: The entry continues through several logical and exegetical senses; only the distinguishing core clause is excerpted here.

records.title: zann
records.ar: والظن تجويز أمرين أحدهما أظهر من الآخر عند المجوز
records.en: Ẓann is taking two alternatives as possible while one of them appears more likely than the other to the person weighing them.
records.body: Supplementary later juristic definition; included as a comparative technical definition, not falsely classified as a historical lexical dictionary.
